houmtsoukdjerba.d: The main town and capital of Djerba, situated on the site of an ancient city. It features a medina, traditional souks and old fondouks.
houmtsoukdjerba.a: The capital of Djerba: medina, traditional souks and old fondouks.
houmtsoukdjerba.c: Stroll through the souks in the morning or evening, when the heat has subsided.

guellaladjerba.d: A village in southern Djerba, a historic centre for pottery thanks to its clay deposits. A pottery tradition dating back to antiquity, with workshops and cave kilns.
guellaladjerba.a: A village in southern Djerba, a historic centre for pottery, with workshops and cave kilns.
guellaladjerba.c: Visit a potter’s workshop; the shops are concentrated along the main road.

mosqueedelmaydjerba.d: A fortified Ibadite mosque in the centre of Djerba, with whitewashed walls and a stocky minaret. Listed as a historic monument in 1928, it serves the defensive role typical of the island’s mosques.
mosqueedelmaydjerba.a: Fortified Ibadite mosque with whitewashed walls and a stocky minaret, listed since 1928.
mosqueedelmaydjerba.c: Be sure to admire the fortified exterior; the interior may be reserved for worshippers.

mosqueefadhloundjerba.d: A 14th-century Ibadite mosque on the outskirts of Midoun, with the simple, fortified architecture typical of Djerba. Listed in 2022.
mosqueefadhloundjerba.a: A 14th-century Ibadite mosque with simple, fortified architecture, on the outskirts of Midoun.
mosqueefadhloundjerba.c: A beautiful, isolated white silhouette: ideal for photographing in soft light.

erriadhharaseghiradjerba.d: A village south of Houmt Souk, a former neighbourhood with a strong Jewish community (Hara Sghira). Home to the Ghriba Synagogue and the Djerbahood murals (2014).
erriadhharaseghiradjerba.a: A former neighbourhood with a strong Jewish community, home to the Ghriba Synagogue and the Djerbahood street murals (2014).
erriadhharaseghiradjerba.c: Wander through the narrow streets on foot to discover the murals; go early in the morning for the best light.

tamezret.d: A Berber village on the slopes of one of the highest peaks of the Matmata Mountains (~480 m), about 40 km south-west of Gabès. An Amazigh-speaking community (Chelha).
tamezret.a: A Berber village on the slopes of one of the highest peaks of the Matmata Mountains, home to an Amazigh-speaking community (Chelha).
tamezret.c: Panoramic view of the mountains: climb up to the upper village for the view; bring water with you.

zraoua.d: Berber village perched on a plateau in the Matmata Mountains (Nouvelle Matmata, Gabès). The inhabitants migrated to a village on the plain in the late 1970s.
zraoua.a: A Berber village perched on a plateau in the Matmata Mountains, partly deserted since the late 1970s.
zraoua.c: Arid mountainous area: bring water and sturdy footwear.

taoujout.d: A Berber village in the Matmata Mountains (Gabès), near Tamezret and Zraoua, where the Chelha Amazigh dialect is traditionally spoken.
taoujout.a: A Berber village in the Matmata Mountains, near Tamezret and Zraoua, with an Amazigh-speaking tradition (Chelha).
taoujout.c: Best combined with a visit to Tamezret; the mountain road requires careful driving.

benikhedache.d: The town and administrative centre of Medenine (~30 km to the west), between Jebel Dahar and the Grand Erg Oriental. Ksour, a fortified granary and an underground mosque.
benikhedache.a: A market town between Jebel Dahar and the Grand Erg, surrounded by ksour, a fortified granary and an underground mosque.
benikhedache.c: A good base for a tour of the ksours; make sure you stock up on water and fuel before heading off-road.

zaouiamosqueesidiboulbabagabes.d: The Sidi Boulbaba zaouïa-mosque complex, dedicated to Abu Lubaba al-Ansari, companion of the Prophet and patron saint of Gabès. It houses the Gabès Ethnographic Museum.
zaouiamosqueesidiboulbabagabes.a: A complex dedicated to Sidi Boulbaba, a companion of the Prophet and the patron saint of Gabès, housing the ethnographic museum.
zaouiamosqueesidiboulbabagabes.c: Appropriate attire; combine your visit with a trip to the adjoining ethnographic museum.

elhammagabes.d: A thermal oasis town some 30 km west of Gabès, renowned since ancient times for its hot springs which supply its hammams.
elhammagabes.a: A thermal oasis town renowned since ancient times for its hot springs which feed the hammams.
elhammagabes.c: The springs are very hot: check which pools are open to visitors.

lignemareth.d: A system of fortifications in southern Tunisia built by the French to face Italian-occupied Libya, captured by the Axis powers in 1942–1943. Breached by the British 8th Army in March 1943. Approximate coordinates.
lignemareth.a: Remains of fortifications in southern Tunisia, breached by the British 8th Army in March 1943.
lignemareth.c: Landmarks scattered across the plain: a guide or the Mareth Museum can help locate them.

ouledelhadefmedinadetozeur.d: The historic quarter of Tozeur, famous for its clay-brick (toub) architecture featuring geometric relief patterns. Medieval medina.
ouledelhadefmedinadetozeur.a: Medieval quarter famous for its clay-brick (toub) façades featuring geometric relief patterns.
ouledelhadefmedinadetozeur.c: Stroll through the shaded alleyways on foot, preferably in the morning or late in the day.

ongjmelmosespadecorstarwars.d: Abandoned Star Wars film set near Nefta (Tozeur), the fictional spaceport of Mos Espa, near the Ong Jmel rock, shaped like a camel’s neck.
ongjmelmosespadecorstarwars.a: Abandoned Mos Espa film set in the dunes, near the Ong Jmel rock, shaped like a camel’s neck.
ongjmelmosespadecorstarwars.c: Access via a track through the sand: a 4x4 is recommended, and visit at sunrise or sunset for the best light.

kebili.d: Capital of the Kebili governorate in the Nefzaoua region, one of the oldest oases in Tunisia and North Africa, near Chott el-Jerid. Deglet Nour dates.
kebili.a: Capital of the Nefzaoua region, one of the oldest oases in North Africa, near the Chott el-Jerid, renowned for its Deglet Nour dates.
kebili.c: A good base from which to explore the chott and the desert; intense heat in summer.

ksarlemsalimisa.d: A remarkably well-preserved 6th-century Byzantine fortress, set amongst the ruins of the ancient Roman-Berber city of Limisa. In Oueslatia (Kairouan), on the border with Siliana, it overlooks the valley with its almost intact large-stone walls.
ksarlemsalimisa.a: A remarkably well-preserved 6th-century Byzantine fortress, with its almost intact large-stone walls overlooking the valley, set amongst the ruins of Limisa.
ksarlemsalimisa.c: Site on the outskirts of Siliana (Oueslatia area): the fortress can be explored in under an hour and offers a fine view of the valley.

vicusmaracitanusksartoualzammel.d: An ancient site in the governorate of Siliana, approximately 15 km south-west of Siliana, identified as Vicus Maracitanus. A two-storey Numidian-Roman mausoleum with a pilastered façade stands within its necropolises. Linked to the question of the location of Zama.
vicusmaracitanusksartoualzammel.a: A two-storey Numidian-Roman mausoleum with a pilaster-flanked façade, situated in the necropolises of this site linked to the question of Zama.
vicusmaracitanusksartoualzammel.c: Approximately 15 km south-west of Siliana; a rural site to be located using precise coordinates.

avittabibbahenchirbouftis.d: Roman city of Africa Proconsularis near Bou Arada, north of Siliana (Henchir Bou Ftis). Former episcopal see; remains of an amphitheatre.
avittabibbahenchirbouftis.a: The scattered remains of the Roman city, including the ruins of an amphitheatre, in the countryside near Bou Arada; a modest site with little infrastructure.
avittabibbahenchirbouftis.c: For archaeology enthusiasts only; you’ll need a car and should ask locals for directions to find it.

bisicalucanahenchirbichga.d: Roman city of Africa Proconsularis (Henchir Bichga, on the outskirts of Bou Arada, north of Siliana). Originally a colony, later a municipality: thermal baths, aqueduct, possible capitol, former bishop’s palace. Approximate coordinates (Pleiades).
bisicalucanahenchirbichga.a: The scattered remains of the ancient Roman colony (thermal baths, traces of an aqueduct) in the countryside near Bou Arada; a modest site now in ruins.
bisicalucanahenchirbichga.c: Site poorly signposted, suitable for experienced visitors; best combined with a visit to nearby Avitta Bibba.

grandemosqueedenabeul.d: The Great Mosque of Nabeul, listed as a historic monument since 3 March 1915.
grandemosqueedenabeul.a: The Great Mosque of Nabeul, listed as a historic monument since 1915.
grandemosqueedenabeul.c: Well worth a visit whilst strolling through the medina of Nabeul; modest dress is required.

mosqueesidiachournabeul.d: The Sidi Achour Mosque in Nabeul, listed as a historic monument since 3 March 1915.
mosqueesidiachournabeul.a: The historic mosque in Nabeul, listed as a historic monument since 1915.
mosqueesidiachournabeul.c: Mainly an exterior visit; best included as part of a stroll through the medina.

sanctuairedethinissut.d: Punic-Roman sanctuary dedicated to Baal Hammon and Tanit, at Bir Bou Rekba near Hammamet. Terracotta statues at the Bardo.
sanctuairedethinissut.a: Punic-Roman sanctuary dedicated to Baal Hammon and Tanit, at Bir Bou Rekba near Hammamet; its terracotta statues are housed in the Bardo Museum.
sanctuairedethinissut.c: On site, the remains are sparse; the main statues can be seen at the Bardo in Tunis.

templecapitolindetubernuc.d: Ancient Capitoline temple at Tubernuc (Soliman/Grombalia region), known locally as the great Byzantine monument with three gates.
templecapitolindetubernuc.a: Ancient Capitoline temple known locally as the ‘Great Monument with Three Doors’, in the Soliman/Grombalia region.
templecapitolindetubernuc.c: A remote and largely undeveloped site; ask for directions on site to find it.

museedarkhadijahammamet.d: A museum housed in a traditional Hammamet residence.
museedarkhadijahammamet.a: A museum housed in a traditional Hammamet residence, showcasing local architecture and decorative arts.
museedarkhadijahammamet.c: A short visit to combine with a tour of Hammamet’s medina.
museedarkhadijahammamet.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

missuasiteantiquedesididaoud.d: The ancient archaeological site of Missua, at Sidi Daoud on Cape Bon. Wikidata coordinates are of low accuracy (~1 km) and approximate.
missuasiteantiquedesididaoud.a: Ancient Punic and Roman ruins at Sidi Daoud, on the north coast of Cap Bon.
missuasiteantiquedesididaoud.c: Location is imprecise and the site is poorly developed; best suited to enthusiasts.

herglahorreacaelia.d: A small white coastal town in the Gulf of Hammamet, on the site of the Roman town of Horrea Caelia. Medina featuring the Sidi Bou Mendil Mosque.
herglahorreacaelia.a: The white village perched on the cliff; the Sidi Bou Mendil Mosque; the narrow streets overlooking the sea and the old mat-weaving workshop.
herglahorreacaelia.c: A picturesque stop-off between Sousse and Hammamet; beautiful views out to sea from the edge of the plateau.

enfidaenfidaville.d: A town in the Sahel near the ancient site of Uppenna. Museum of early Christian mosaics; Commonwealth war cemetery (1942–1943).
enfidaenfidaville.a: A town in the Sahel region near ancient Uppenna; a museum of early Christian mosaics and a Commonwealth war cemetery from the 1942–1943 campaign.
enfidaenfidaville.c: The Enfida Museum and the military cemetery are the two main points of interest.

museedenfida.d: Former Neo-Romanesque church (1907) converted into a regional museum in 1966. Rich collection of Christian funerary mosaics from Uppenna.
museedenfida.a: A former Neo-Romanesque church dating from 1907, converted into a regional museum, displaying a rich collection of Christian funerary mosaics from Uppenna.
museedenfida.c: Best visited in conjunction with the nearby site of Uppenna, from which the mosaics originate.
museedenfida.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

uppennahenchirchigarnia.d: Ancient site north of Enfida with an early Christian basilica. Source of the famous epigraphic mosaics in the Enfida Museum.
uppennahenchirchigarnia.a: Ancient site north of Enfida with an early Christian basilica, from which the famous epigraphic mosaics in the Enfida Museum originate.
uppennahenchirchigarnia.c: The site is rather bare; a visit is best combined with a trip to the Enfida Museum.

museearcheologiquedesousse.d: A museum housed in the Kasbah of Sousse, home to one of the richest collections of Roman mosaics in Tunisia.
museearcheologiquedesousse.a: Housed in the kasbah, it contains one of the finest collections of Roman mosaics in Tunisia.
museearcheologiquedesousse.c: A must-see in the Sahel for mosaics; best combined with a visit to the kasbah that houses it.
museearcheologiquedesousse.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

msaken.d: A town in the Sahel region south of Sousse: the Great Mosque, the El Aousat Mosque, the Chakir Saheb Ettabaâ Palace (1828) and numerous zaouias.
msaken.a: A town in the Sahel with a rich heritage: the Great Mosque, the El Aousat Mosque, the Chakir Saheb Ettabaâ Palace (1828) and numerous zaouias.
msaken.c: An urban stroll off the beaten track; visits are mainly of the exterior.

kalaakebira.d: A town whose name means ‘great fortress’. The old town centre, ‘El Ksar’, was founded under the Aghlabids and was once surrounded by a rampart.
kalaakebira.a: A city whose name means ‘great fortress’, centred around the old town ‘El Ksar’, founded under the Aghlabids and once surrounded by a rampart.
kalaakebira.c: A nearby stopover from Sousse for those interested in the ancient fabric of the Sahel.

akouda.d: A town north-west of Sousse, characterised by the minaret of its Great Mosque.
akouda.a: A town north-west of Sousse, characterised by the minaret of its Great Mosque.
akouda.c: A brief stop; of interest mainly for the minaret and the old town centre.

synagoguedemoknine.d: The former synagogue of the Jewish community of Moknine, a testament to Tunisia’s Jewish heritage.
synagoguedemoknine.a: Former synagogue of the Jewish community of Moknine, a testament to the Jewish-Tunisian heritage of the Sahel.
synagoguedemoknine.c: Check locally for visiting arrangements, as the building is not always open.

museearcheologiqueetethnographiquedemokn.d: Museum of Punic artefacts and collections of folk art and traditions (textiles, jewellery, crafts). Opened in 2007.
museearcheologiqueetethnographiquedemokn.a: Museum (2007) combining Punic artefacts with collections of folk art and traditions: textiles, jewellery and local crafts.
museearcheologiqueetethnographiquedemokn.c: A good insight into the material culture of the Sahel; well worth visiting alongside the Moknine synagogue.
museearcheologiqueetethnographiquedemokn.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

museedesartsettraditionspopulairesdemona.d: Monastir Museum of Folk Arts and Traditions, in the medina (established in 1985).
museedesartsettraditionspopulairesdemona.a: Museum of Folk Arts and Traditions located in the medina of Monastir (established in 1985).
museedesartsettraditionspopulairesdemona.c: A visit to include as part of a tour of Monastir’s medina and ribat.
museedesartsettraditionspopulairesdemona.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

rempartsdemonastir.d: The ancient walls of Monastir’s medina, separate from the ribat.
rempartsdemonastir.a: The ancient walls of the Monastir medina, separate from the ribat, marking the historic layout of the town.
rempartsdemonastir.c: To be explored whilst walking through the medina during a visit to the ribat.

mausoleeomarmakhloufmonastir.d: Zaouïa and mausoleum in the medina of Monastir, a traditional place of worship.
mausoleeomarmakhloufmonastir.a: Zaouïa and mausoleum in the medina of Monastir, a traditional place of worship.
mausoleeomarmakhloufmonastir.c: A small building worth seeing whilst passing through the medina; please respect the religious nature of the site.

ruspina.d: Ancient Punic and later Roman city corresponding to present-day Monastir, mentioned in ancient sources (Caesar’s Civil War).
ruspina.a: An ancient Punic and later Roman city corresponding to present-day Monastir, mentioned in ancient sources (Caesar’s Civil War); very few remains.
ruspina.c: More of a historical landmark than a site open to visitors, as the modern city has built over the ancient one.

tataouinefoumtataouine.d: Capital of the Tataouine governorate, a former garrison town of the Protectorate, and gateway to the ksour of Dahar.
tataouinefoumtataouine.a: A former garrison town during the Protectorate, and the gateway to the ksour of the Dahar.
tataouinefoumtataouine.c: Starting point for tours to the ksours: make sure you have plenty of water and fuel.

ksarouledaoun.d: The semi-circular Ksar a Ghorfas near Maztouria, with 96 to 220 ghorfas spread over two to three storeys; restored in 2007.
ksarouledaoun.a: A semi-circular ksar with ghorfas near Maztouria, restored, with two to three storeys.
ksarouledaoun.c: A short stop; the light at the end of the day is most flattering for photos.

ksarelkedim.d: Fortified ksar in the governorate of Tataouine, a listed monument, attributed to the Zenete Berbers.
ksarelkedim.a: A listed fortified ksar, attributed to the Zenete Berbers, in the Tataouine governorate.
ksarelkedim.c: A modest site to include in a tour of the ksours with a local guide.

ksardghaghra.d: Berber ksar (fortified granary) in the Tataouine governorate.
ksardghaghra.a: Berber ksar (fortified granary) in the Tataouine governorate.
ksardghaghra.c: A quick visit; can be combined with the neighbouring ksours of Dahar.

ksarjelidetksarboujlida.d: A ksar forming part of the Ksour Jelidet complex, a listed Berber fortified granary.
ksarjelidetksarboujlida.a: A listed Berber fort-granary, forming part of the Ksour Jelidet complex.
ksarjelidetksarboujlida.c: Access via tracks: a local guide makes it easier to find.

ksarbenighedir.d: Ksar a Ghorfas in the north of the Tataouine governorate, in the area of the fortified granaries of Dahar.
ksarbenighedir.a: Ksar a Ghorfas in the north of Tataouine, in the area of the fortified granaries of Dahar.
ksarbenighedir.c: A short stop; worth including in a tour of the ksours.

ksarbenimhiraelataya.d: Rectangular ksar (150x70 m) on a hill in the Djeffara, ~160 ghorfas.
ksarbenimhiraelataya.a: A rectangular ksar (150 x 70 m) on a hill in the Djeffara region, with around 160 ghorfas.
ksarbenimhiraelataya.c: A pleasant vantage point for watching the sunset; bring water.

ksarbenimhirazorgane.d: A parallelogram-shaped ksar (120x80 m) near Beni Mhira, with 170 to 250 ghorfas on two storeys.
ksarbenimhirazorgane.a: A parallelogram-shaped ksar (120x80 m) with 170 to 250 ghorfas spread over two storeys.
ksarbenimhirazorgane.c: Best visited in conjunction with the other Beni Mhira ksar; expect hot weather.

remadatillibari.d: A southern town near the Libyan border, on the site of the ancient Roman fort of Tillibari (limes).
remadatillibari.a: A southern town on the site of the ancient Roman fort of Tillibari (Limes), near the Libyan border.
remadatillibari.c: Remote border area: check access details and carry plenty of water with you.

dehiba.d: A town in the east of the Tataouine governorate, a border crossing with Libya.
dehiba.a: A town in the east of Tataouine, a border crossing with Libya.
dehiba.c: Mainly of interest as a transit point; check the conditions in the border area.

medeninevilleetksour.d: Capital of the Medenine governorate, famous for its ksour a ghorfas (collective storehouses of the Berber tribes).
medeninevilleetksour.a: Capital city famous for its ksour a ghorfas, ancient communal storehouses of the Berber tribes.
medeninevilleetksour.c: A few restored ghorfas can be visited in the town; a convenient stopover on the way to the ksour of Dahar.

zarzisgergis.d: A coastal town in the south-east, a seaside resort fringed by olive groves, on the site of ancient Gergis.
zarzisgergis.a: A seaside resort flanked by olive groves, on the site of ancient Gergis.
zarzisgergis.c: Beaches and coastal relaxation; can be combined with a visit to nearby Djerba.

bengardane.d: A town in the south-east near the Libyan border, an important cross-border trading centre.
bengardane.a: A town in the south-east, a major cross-border commercial centre close to Libya.
bengardane.c: Of mainly commercial and transit interest; check the latest news regarding the border area.

ajimdjerba.d: A coastal town in the west of Djerba, the main ferry link to the mainland and a former sponge-fishing port.
ajimdjerba.a: A port in the west of Djerba, the main ferry link to the mainland and a former sponge-fishing port.
ajimdjerba.c: The ferry connects Djerba to the mainland: allow for waiting times during peak hours.

sedouikechdjerba.d: A village in central Djerba, one of the few places where the Djerba Berber language is still spoken.
sedouikechdjerba.a: A village in central Djerba, one of the few places where the island’s Berber culture still survives.
sedouikechdjerba.c: A peaceful retreat in the heart of the island, far from the hustle and bustle of the seaside resorts.

midoundjerba.d: Djerba’s second-largest town by population, the centre of the north-east of the island.
midoundjerba.a: Djerba’s second-largest town, a lively hub in the north-east of the island.
midoundjerba.c: Famous weekly market: arrive early to soak up the atmosphere and avoid the heat.

mahboubinedjerba.d: A village in south-eastern Djerba, known for its Ottoman-inspired El Kateb Mosque.
mahboubinedjerba.a: A village in south-eastern Djerba, known for its Ottoman-inspired El Kateb Mosque.
mahboubinedjerba.c: A short stop to admire the mosque; please dress appropriately when visiting.

elkantaradjerba.d: A town in south-eastern Djerba, situated on the site of the Roman road linking the island to the mainland towards Zarzis.
elkantaradjerba.a: A town situated on the site of the Roman road linking the island to the mainland towards Zarzis.
elkantaradjerba.c: A crossing point on the road: convenient for reaching the mainland.

boughrara.d: A village on the mainland near the ancient city of Gightis, on the coast facing Djerba.
boughrara.a: A coastal village on the mainland, near the ancient city of Gightis, facing Djerba.
boughrara.c: Best combined with a visit to the nearby ancient site of Gightis.

medinadegabesjara.d: The historic centre of Gabès, an oasis town in the gulf, with the old quarters of Petite and Grande Jara, on the site of ancient Tacapae.
medinadegabesjara.a: The historic heart of the oasis town on the Gulf, with the old quarters of Petite and Grande Jara, on the site of ancient Tacapae.
medinadegabesjara.c: Stroll through the medina and the neighbouring oasis, avoiding the midday heat.

ghannouch.d: Municipality and administrative centre of the Gabès governorate, on the Gulf to the north of the city.
ghannouch.a: A municipality on the Gulf of Gabès, to the north of the city.
ghannouch.c: Ordinary town: of limited interest to visitors; more of a stopover.

oudhref.d: A town and sub-prefecture of the Gabès governorate, north-west of Gabès.
oudhref.a: A town and sub-prefecture north-west of Gabès.
oudhref.c: A stop-off point; little of major tourist interest.

elmetouia.d: An oasis settlement and sub-prefecture of the Gabès Governorate, to the north of the city.
elmetouia.a: An oasis town north of Gabès, in the Gulf Oasis.
elmetouia.c: A cool stroll under the palm trees is possible during the hottest part of the day.

nouvellematmata.d: A new town built on the Aradh plateau to resettle the Berber populations from the Matmata mountains.
nouvellematmata.a: A new town built on the Aradh plateau to resettle the Berber people from the Matmata mountains.
nouvellematmata.c: A stopover on the way to historic Matmata and its cave dwellings.

chenininahalgabes.d: A village and coastal oasis to the south-west of Gabès (date palms, henna). Distinct from the Berber village of Chenini in Tataouine.
chenininahalgabes.a: A village and coastal oasis south-west of Gabès (date palms, henna); distinct from the Berber village of Chenini in Tataouine.
chenininahalgabes.c: A shaded stroll through the oasis; not to be confused with Chenini in Tataouine.

mareth.d: A town between Gabès and Medenine, which gave its name to the Mareth Line (1930s).
mareth.a: A town that gave its name to the Mareth Line; a local museum commemorates the battle of 1943.
mareth.c: The Mareth Line Museum helps visitors to understand the surrounding ruins.

zarat.d: A coastal town in the governorate of Gabès, south of Gabès, with a fishing harbour.
zarat.a: A coastal town south of Gabès, with a fishing harbour.
zarat.c: Small-town harbour atmosphere; of mainly local interest.

batailledelouedakarit.d: A battle during the Tunisian Campaign along the Akarit wadi, north of Gabès, in the area between the sea and the chotts.
batailledelouedakarit.a: A memorial site for the battle of April 1943, in the area between the sea and the chotts north of Gabès.
batailledelouedakarit.c: A memorial site with no significant development: of mainly historical interest.

bouchemma.d: A town and municipality in the Governorate of Gabès (West Gabès), within the Gabès Oasis.
bouchemma.a: A locality in the Gabès Oasis (West Gabès).
bouchemma.c: A peaceful oasis stopover; little of major tourist interest.

elguettar.d: An oasis town south-east of Gafsa, famous for the El Guettar Hermaion (Mousterian/Aterian) and the Battle of El Guettar (1943).
elguettar.a: An oasis town famous for the El Guettar Hermaion (Mousterian/Aterian) and the battle of 1943.
elguettar.c: The prehistoric context is best understood through the nearby Gafsa Museum.

metlaoui.d: A mining town in the Gafsa Basin (phosphate), the departure point for the Lezard Rouge train to the Selja Gorges.
metlaoui.a: A mining town in the Gafsa Basin, the starting point for the Lezard Rouge train to the Selja Gorges.
metlaoui.c: Book the Lezard Rouge in advance; water is essential in summer.

redeyef.d: A phosphate mining town in the Gafsa Basin, the epicentre of the 2008 social movement.
redeyef.a: A phosphate mining town in the Gafsa Basin, the epicentre of the 2008 social movement.
redeyef.c: Of mainly historical and social interest; a stop on the Lezard Rouge line.

moularesoumelaraies.d: Phosphate mining town (Oum El Araies) about 50 km from Gafsa, near the Algerian border.
moularesoumelaraies.a: Phosphate mining town about 50 km from Gafsa, near the Algerian border.

mdhilla.d: Phosphate mining town in the governorate of Gafsa (CPG plant).
mdhilla.a: Phosphate mining town in the governorate of Gafsa, home to the CPG plant.
mdhilla.c: Industrial town: of little interest to visitors.

sened.d: A village and the administrative centre of the delegation, situated about 50 km east of Gafsa, known for its ancient Berber dialect.
sened.a: A village about 50 km east of Gafsa, known for its ancient Berber dialect.
sened.c: A peaceful stopover; of interest mainly for its culture and language.

belkhir.d: A town and the administrative centre of the Gafsa governorate.
belkhir.a: Administrative centre of the Gafsa governorate.
belkhir.c: A place of passage: little major tourist interest.

sidiaich.d: A town and the administrative centre of the Gafsa Governorate, situated to the north of Gafsa, in a region of mountainous terrain and mountain oases.
sidiaich.a: A town north of Gafsa, in a region of rugged terrain and mountain oases.
sidiaich.c: Possible starting point for trips to the surrounding mountain oases.

degache.d: An oasis town in the Jerid region north of Tozeur, on the edge of the Chott el-Jerid (deglet nour).
degache.a: An oasis town in the Jerid on the edge of the Chott el-Jerid, renowned for its deglet nour dates.
degache.c: A stop-off on the way to the chott; a stroll through the palm grove in the cooler hours of the day.

hazoua.d: A small oasis town in the governorate of Tozeur, close to the Algerian border.
hazoua.a: A small oasis town near the Algerian border, in the governorate of Tozeur.
hazoua.c: Remote border town: make sure you have enough water and fuel.

blidet.d: Oasis village in the governorate of Kebili, in the Nefzaoua oasis region.
blidet.a: An oasis village in the Nefzaoua region, within the Kebili oasis region.
blidet.c: A peaceful oasis stopover; the shade of the palm trees is a welcome relief in summer.

jemna.d: An oasis town in the Nefzaoua region, renowned for its springs and date production; it features an old mosque housing an ancient library.
jemna.a: An oasis town in the Nefzaoua region, renowned for its springs and dates, with an old mosque housing an ancient library.
jemna.c: A stroll through the palm grove; intense heat in summer.

zaafrane.d: Oasis village in the governorate of Kebili, gateway to the Grand Erg Oriental and centre of the Adhara nomads.
zaafrane.a: Oasis village, gateway to the Grand Erg Oriental and centre of the Adhara nomads.
zaafrane.c: Starting point for excursions into the dunes: 4x4 or camel treks at sunrise/sunset.

sabria.d: Oasis village in the Kebili governorate, nestled amongst the first major dunes, around 30 km from Douz.
sabria.a: An oasis village nestled amongst the first major dunes, about thirty kilometres from Douz.
sabria.c: Saharan setting: come and admire the dunes in the low light of morning or evening.

elfaouar.d: Town and administrative centre of the Kebili governorate, a Saharan oasis settlement.
elfaouar.a: A Saharan oasis town and the administrative centre of the Kebili governorate.
elfaouar.c: Starting point for trips into the desert; extreme heat in summer, so set off early.

souklahad.d: Oasis town and administrative centre of the Nefzaoua district, situated ~15 km north-west of Kebili, on the edge of the Chott el-Jerid.
souklahad.a: An oasis town in the Nefzaoua region on the edge of the Chott el-Jerid, about fifteen km from Kebili.
souklahad.c: Oasis stopover; combine with a crossing of the chott.

telmine.d: The village of Kebili Nord on the edge of the Chott el-Jerid, near the ancient site of Turris Tamalleni.
telmine.a: A village on the edge of the Chott el-Jerid, close to the ancient site of Turris Tamalleni.
telmine.c: Best combined with a visit to the nearby ruins of Turris Tamalleni.

turristamallenitelmine.d: Ancient site near Telmine, at the western end of the Limes Tripolitanus: a Roman fort which later became a municipality under Hadrian, and the centre of the Nybgenii.
turristamallenitelmine.a: Ancient site at the western end of the Limes: a Roman fort, later a municipality under Hadrian, and the centre of the Nybgenii tribe.
turristamallenitelmine.c: Modest open-air ruins: a guide helps to interpret them; bring water and a hat.

fatnassa.d: Oasis village in the Souk Lahad district, on the southern shore of Chott el-Jerid.
fatnassa.a: Oasis village on the southern shore of Chott el-Jerid, in the Souk Lahad district.
fatnassa.c: A peaceful oasis stop; the shade of the palm trees is welcome in summer.

centenariumtibubuciksartarcine.d: Late Roman fort on the edge of the Grand Erg Oriental, part of the Limes Tripolitanus. UNESCO Tentative List.
centenariumtibubuciksartarcine.a: Late Roman fort (c. 297–305) on the edge of the Grand Erg Oriental, part of the Limes; on the UNESCO Tentative List.
centenariumtibubuciksartarcine.c: Access via a Saharan track: 4x4 vehicle and guide essential; ample water required.

bordjlazaritgharelmelh.d: The Ottoman fort at Ghar el Melh, one of the three bordjs near the ancient port of Porto Farina.
bordjlazaritgharelmelh.a: The third of the 17th-century Ottoman forts at Ghar el Melh, near the ancient port of Porto Farina.
bordjlazaritgharelmelh.c: Completes the tour of the three bordjs; allow half a day for the entire site and the lagoon.

pontmobiledebizerte.d: The iconic bascule bridge spanning the Bizerte Canal, linking the city to Zarzouna.
pontmobiledebizerte.a: The bascule bridge, built in 1980, spanning the Bizerte Canal and linking the city to Zarzouna, is an iconic feature of the urban landscape.
pontmobiledebizerte.c: A sight worth seeing from the quays, particularly when the bridge is raised to allow ships to pass.

mosqueerebaabizerte.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Bizerte.
mosqueerebaabizerte.a: Historic Ottoman-era mosque in the heart of Bizerte’s medina.
mosqueerebaabizerte.c: Appropriate attire is required; best viewed whilst strolling through the medina, as there is no specific route to follow.

zaouiasidielarbirasjebel.d: The zaouïa and mausoleum at Ras Jebel, a place of local worship.
zaouiasidielarbirasjebel.a: The zaouïa and mausoleum of Sidi El Arbi at Ras Jebel, a place of local worship.
zaouiasidielarbirasjebel.c: A small place of worship: a brief visit, best combined with a trip to the Andalusian villages along the coast (Raf Raf, Metline).

museeoceanographiquedebizerte.d: Museum of Marine Fauna and Flora, near the old port of Bizerte.
museeoceanographiquedebizerte.a: Collections of Mediterranean marine flora and fauna, on display near the old harbour.
museeoceanographiquedebizerte.c: A short, sheltered visit, ideal in bad weather; best combined with a stroll around the old harbour.
museeoceanographiquedebizerte.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

museenationaldutique.d: Archaeological Museum of the Punic and Roman remains at the site of Utica.
museenationaldutique.a: The Punic and Roman archaeological collections from the site of Utica: artefacts, statues and mosaics.
museenationaldutique.c: Best visited just before or after the nearby site of Utica; allow about 1 hour.
museenationaldutique.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

ecomuseedelichkeul.d: Ichkeul National Park Ecomuseum (fauna, flora, geology), at the foot of Djebel Ichkeul.
ecomuseedelichkeul.a: Exhibits on the flora, fauna and geology of Ichkeul National Park, at the foot of Djebel Ichkeul.
ecomuseedelichkeul.c: The ideal starting point for a visit to the park; start here to get an understanding of the site before climbing Djebel Ichkeul.
ecomuseedelichkeul.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

maisondelacascadeutique.d: Roman domus at the Utica site, decorated with mosaics and featuring a pool.
maisondelacascadeutique.a: The Roman domus, adorned with mosaics and featuring a pool, is one of the finest residential complexes at the Utica site.
maisondelacascadeutique.c: Included in the tour of the Utica site; take a look at the mosaics in situ around the pool.

eglisesaintalexandrenevskidebizerte.d: Russian Orthodox Church in Bizerte, built by sailors from the Russian fleet who took refuge there after 1920.
eglisesaintalexandrenevskidebizerte.a: The Russian Orthodox church dating from 1939, built by sailors from the Russian fleet who took refuge in Bizerte after 1920.
eglisesaintalexandrenevskidebizerte.c: A small, distinctive building in the town; a brief visit, best combined with a tour of Bizerte’s town centre.

sejnane.d: A rural town known for its pottery, hand-modelled by women, inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2018.
sejnane.a: The craft of hand-modelled pottery by local women, inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2018, and the town’s rural atmosphere.
sejnane.c: Look out for potters and cooperatives to view and buy traditional ceramics; best combined with a visit to the nearby wetlands.

rafraf.d: A coastal town famous for its beach and its Andalusian heritage, facing Pilau Island.
rafraf.a: The large beach facing Pilau Island and the coastal town’s Andalusian heritage.
rafraf.c: Primarily a seaside destination: best visited in the warmer months and combined with a visit to the nearby Cape Sidi Ali El Mekki.

metline.d: A coastal village of Andalusian origin to the north-east of Bizerte (maritime and wine-growing heritage).
metline.a: The coastal village of Andalusian origin to the north-east of Bizerte, with its maritime and wine-growing heritage.
metline.c: A peaceful stopover to combine with Raf Raf and the other Andalusian villages along the coast.

elalia.d: A town of Andalusian origin renowned for its chechia craftsmanship and textile traditions.
elalia.a: The Andalusian town renowned for its chechia craftsmanship and textile traditions.
elalia.c: Discover the chechia workshops; a short visit, best combined with a tour of the region’s other Andalusian towns.

petitemosqueedebeja.d: The historic mosque in the medina of Beja, more modest than the Great Mosque.
petitemosqueedebeja.a: A historic mosque, more modest than the Great Mosque, in the heart of the medina of Beja.
petitemosqueedebeja.c: Well worth a look whilst strolling through the medina; smart dress is required.

eglisenotredamedurosairedebeja.d: Catholic church built during the Protectorate era in Beja.
eglisenotredamedurosairedebeja.a: The Catholic church, built during the Protectorate era, bears witness to Béja’s colonial heritage.
eglisenotredamedurosairedebeja.c: A brief stop in the town centre, well worth including in your tour of Béja.

chaouachsua.d: The hilltop village of ancient Sua, dominated by a Byzantine fortress, with Roman and Christian ruins. North of Teboursouk.
chaouachsua.a: The hilltop village of ancient Sua, dominated by a Byzantine fortress, with Roman and Christian ruins.
chaouachsua.c: Mountain road north of Teboursouk: combine with a visit to neighbouring Toukabeur; wear sturdy footwear for the climb.

toukabeurthuccabor.d: A hilltop village on the site of ancient Thuccabor, with Roman ruins and an ancient mosque. A heritage site alongside Chaouach.
toukabeurthuccabor.a: The hilltop village on the site of ancient Thuccabor, with its Roman ruins and ancient mosque, forming a heritage pairing with Chaouach.
toukabeurthuccabor.c: Best visited in combination with Chaouach as part of the same excursion; a vehicle is required for the ridge roads.

teboursouk.d: The historic town of ancient Thubursicum Bure (medina, kasbah, ramparts), gateway to Dougga.
teboursouk.a: The historic town of ancient Thubursicum Bure: medina, kasbah and ramparts, gateway to Dougga.
teboursouk.c: A convenient stopover before or after Dougga; make it a stop for amenities and to explore the medina.

museedeteboursouk.d: Archaeological museum housing collections from the region’s ancient sites, notably Dougga.
museedeteboursouk.a: Archaeological collections from the region’s ancient sites, notably Dougga.
museedeteboursouk.c: A short visit to complement your trip to Dougga; check opening times on arrival.
museedeteboursouk.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on arrival.

mosqueedebabteboursouktestour.d: The Andalusian-style Testour Mosque, near the Teboursouk Gate, a legacy of the Moriscos.
mosqueedebabteboursouktestour.a: The Andalusian-style mosque near the Teboursouk Gate, part of Testour’s Moorish heritage.
mosqueedebabteboursouktestour.c: Well worth seeing whilst strolling through Testour, along with the Great Andalusian Mosque; appropriate dress required.

zaouiasidinaceurtestour.d: The zaouïa and mausoleum of the saint Sidi Naceur in Testour, part of the Andalusian heritage.
zaouiasidinaceurtestour.a: The zaouïa and mausoleum of the saint Sidi Naceur, a testament to Testour’s Andalusian heritage.
zaouiasidinaceurtestour.c: A brief stop to combine with the other Andalusian monuments in Testour.

medjezelbab.d: A strategic town on the Medjerda, a historic crossing point and a key location in the Tunisian campaign (1942–1943).
medjezelbab.a: The strategic town on the Medjerda, its historic crossing point and traces of the 1942–1943 Tunisian campaign.
medjezelbab.c: To be combined with the Ottoman bridge and the Commonwealth Memorial; a stopover for military and river history.

memorialdemedjezelbab.d: Commonwealth Memorial honouring soldiers from the Tunisian Campaign who are missing and have no known grave.
memorialdemedjezelbab.a: The Commonwealth Memorial honouring soldiers who went missing during the Tunisian Campaign and have no known grave.
memorialdemedjezelbab.c: A place of reflection; a quiet, short visit, to be combined with the bridge and the town of Medjez el-Bab.

nefza.d: A town in the north-west of the Beja governorate, a forested and mountainous region close to the Kroumirie.
nefza.a: The forested and mountainous landscape of the north-west of the Beja governorate, on the edge of the Kroumirie region.
nefza.c: Above all, a nature stop: best combined with a visit to Djebel Khroufa and the surrounding forests in spring.

theatredebullaregia.d: The Roman theatre at the archaeological site of Bulla Regia, near Jendouba.
theatredebullaregia.a: The Roman theatre at the Bulla Regia site, where the tiers of seating and the orchestra are still clearly visible.
theatredebullaregia.c: Included in the tour of Bulla Regia; well worth a visit whilst exploring the whole site.

thermesdejuliamemmiabullaregia.d: The Great Public Baths of Bulla Regia (2nd century), among the city’s most imposing monuments.
thermesdejuliamemmiabullaregia.a: The large public baths dating from the 2nd century, among the most imposing monuments in Bulla Regia thanks to their well-preserved walls and vaults.
thermesdejuliamemmiabullaregia.c: A highlight of the tour of Bulla Regia; look up at the tall structures still standing.

maisondamphitritebullaregia.d: The underground dwelling at Bulla Regia, famous for its mosaic of Amphitrite. Cave-dwelling architecture.
maisondamphitritebullaregia.a: The underground dwelling, famous for its Amphitrite mosaic which remains in situ, is a remarkable example of Bulla Regia’s troglodytic dwellings.
maisondamphitritebullaregia.c: Head down into the underground chamber to admire the mosaic, which is cooler during the hottest part of the day; don’t miss it.

maisondelachassebullaregia.d: Semi-underground Roman dwelling at Bulla Regia, decorated with mosaics, typical of the underground dwellings.
maisondelachassebullaregia.a: The semi-underground Roman house adorned with mosaics, typical of the underground dwellings at Bulla Regia.
maisondelachassebullaregia.c: Combine this with a visit to the neighbouring House of Amphitrite whilst touring the underground villas.

templedapollonbullaregia.d: Roman temple dedicated to Apollo at Bulla Regia; the statues are now in the Bardo Museum.
templedapollonbullaregia.a: The remains of the temple dedicated to Apollo, whose statues are now housed in the Bardo Museum.
templedapollonbullaregia.c: A stop on the Bulla Regia tour; to see the statues, extend your visit to the Bardo Museum in Tunis.

museedebullaregia.d: Site museum displaying artefacts and mosaics from the excavations at Bulla Regia.
museedebullaregia.a: Artefacts and mosaics from the Bulla Regia excavations, on display in the on-site museum.
museedebullaregia.c: Worth visiting alongside the archaeological site; allow about half an hour.
museedebullaregia.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

theatredechemtousimitthus.d: Roman theatre of ancient Simitthus (Chemtou), on the banks of the Medjerda.
theatredechemtousimitthus.a: The Roman theatre of ancient Simitthus, on the banks of the Medjerda.
theatredechemtousimitthus.c: Included in the tour of Chemtou; to be explored alongside the quarries and the museum.

basiliquedechemtou.d: Roman civil basilica of Simitthus, in the heart of the ancient city.
basiliquedechemtou.a: The Roman civil basilica in the heart of the ancient city of Simitthus.
basiliquedechemtou.c: A stop on the Chemtou tour; best visited alongside the nearby theatre and Roman bridge.

museedechemtou.d: Archaeological Museum of Numidian Marble and the Ruins of Simitthus (marble quarries).
museedechemtou.a: The museum dedicated to Numidian yellow marble and the remains of Simitthus, explaining how the quarries were exploited by the Romans.
museedechemtou.c: Start with the museum to understand the site, then explore the quarries; best combined with a visit to Bulla Regia.
museedechemtou.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

museedelamemoirecommunetunisoalgerienneg.d: Ghardimaou Museum dedicated to the shared Tunisian-Algerian history (the struggle for independence).
museedelamemoirecommunetunisoalgerienneg.a: The collections dedicated to the shared Tunisian-Algerian history and the struggle for independence, in Ghardimaou.
museedelamemoirecommunetunisoalgerienneg.c: Historical themed tour near the border; best combined with a visit to the neighbouring Ain Zana nature reserve.
museedelamemoirecommunetunisoalgerienneg.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

cimetieremilitairederasrajel.d: Commonwealth War Graves Cemetery near Tabarka (soldiers from the Tunisian campaign).
cimetieremilitairederasrajel.a: The Commonwealth War Cemetery, where soldiers from the Tunisian campaign are laid to rest, in a well-maintained setting near Tabarka.
cimetieremilitairederasrajel.c: A peaceful place of remembrance; a short stop on the road to Tabarka, to be visited with respect.

henchirbez.d: Ancient archaeological site (henchir) in the north-west of the Kairouan governorate.
henchirbez.a: Ancient archaeological site (henchir) in the north-west of the Kairouan governorate; modest remains.
henchirbez.c: Of mainly archaeological interest: check locally for access details.

elaoujasitedeceramiquesigillee.d: An ancient archaeological site known as the site where sigillata pottery was discovered.
elaoujasitedeceramiquesigillee.a: An ancient site known as the place where sigillata pottery was discovered; the surface remains are not particularly spectacular.

necropoledehaouchtaacha.d: Roman necropolis in the south of the Kairouan governorate.
necropoledehaouchtaacha.a: Roman necropolis in the south of the Kairouan governorate.
necropoledehaouchtaacha.c: An inconspicuous site: you’ll need a guide to find it.

pontaqueducsurlouedcherchira.d: Ancient aqueduct bridge spanning the Cherchira wadi, near Haffouz.
pontaqueducsurlouedcherchira.a: Ancient hydraulic structure spanning the Cherchira wadi, near Haffouz.
pontaqueducsurlouedcherchira.c: Worth a look if you’re travelling through the Haffouz region.

pontromainsurloueddjilf.d: Roman bridge spanning the Djilf wadi, in the Oueslatia region.
pontromainsurloueddjilf.a: Roman bridge spanning the Djilf wadi, in the Oueslatia region.
pontromainsurloueddjilf.c: A quick stop for lovers of Roman architecture, by car.

mausoleesidiamorabbada.d: The Zaouïa of Sidi Amor Abbada (Mosque of the Sabres), 19th century, recognisable by its five fluted domes.
mausoleesidiamorabbada.a: A 19th-century zaouïa known as the Mosque of the Sabres, recognisable by its five fluted domes and its monumental features.
mausoleesidiamorabbada.c: A place of interest to include on a walk around Kairouan; modest dress is appreciated.

mausoleeelouhaichia.d: Zaouïa-mausoleum in the medina of Kairouan.
mausoleeelouhaichia.a: Zaouïa-mausoleum in the medina of Kairouan; a modest monument.
mausoleeelouhaichia.c: Worth a look whilst strolling through the medina.

mausoleesidiabdesselam.d: Zaouïa-mausoleum in the medina of Kairouan.
mausoleesidiabdesselam.a: Zaouïa-mausoleum in the medina of Kairouan; a modest monument.
mausoleesidiabdesselam.c: Worth a look whilst strolling through the medina.

mosqueealmalekkairouan.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosqueealmalekkairouan.a: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosqueealmalekkairouan.c: Place of worship: view from the outside and keep a low profile.

mosqueesikayakairouan.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosqueesikayakairouan.a: The historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosqueesikayakairouan.c: Place of worship: view from the outside and be discreet.

mosqueeellawlibkairouan.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosqueeellawlibkairouan.a: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosqueeellawlibkairouan.c: Place of worship: view from the outside and remain discreet.

eglisedelimmaculeeconceptiondekairouan.d: Catholic church in Kairouan, a legacy of the French Protectorate.
eglisedelimmaculeeconceptiondekairouan.a: Catholic church inherited from the French Protectorate, a testament to the city’s colonial heritage.
eglisedelimmaculeeconceptiondekairouan.c: Check opening times on arrival, as the building is not always open.

museedutapisdekairouan.d: Museum dedicated to Kairouan carpets, in the medina.
museedutapisdekairouan.a: A museum dedicated to Kairouan carpets, an iconic craft of the city.
museedutapisdekairouan.c: A good introduction before visiting the weavers’ workshops in the medina.
museedutapisdekairouan.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); opening times to be checked on arrival.

campdeconcentrationdekondas.d: Former concentration camp in Kondas, Kairouan Governorate.
campdeconcentrationdekondas.a: Site of a former Second World War concentration camp; a place of remembrance with no significant remains.
campdeconcentrationdekondas.c: A site of remembrance rather than a tourist attraction; check locally for details.

museedemahdia.d: Mahdia Archaeological and Ethnographic Museum, separate from Borj el-Kebir.
museedemahdia.a: Mahdia Archaeological and Ethnographic Museum (1997), showcasing the history of the city and its region.
museedemahdia.c: Best combined with a visit to the medina and Borj el-Kebir.
museedemahdia.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

darsghirmahdia.d: Museum housed in a traditional house in the medina of Mahdia.
darsghirmahdia.a: A small museum housed in a traditional house in the medina, showcasing local architecture and arts.
darsghirmahdia.c: A quick stop during a stroll through the medina.

museearcheologiquedesalakta.d: The Salakta Archaeological Museum, showcasing the remains of ancient Sullecthum.
museearcheologiquedesalakta.a: Museum displaying the remains of ancient Sullecthum, including a large mosaic of a lion.
museearcheologiquedesalakta.c: Best visited alongside the nearby Salakta archaeological site.
museearcheologiquedesalakta.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

cimetieremarindemahdia.d: Seaside cemetery on the Mahdia peninsula, overlooking the sea.
cimetieremarindemahdia.a: Historic cemetery facing the sea on the Mahdia peninsula; a peaceful setting by the coast.
cimetieremarindemahdia.c: A place of contemplation: please visit with respect, especially at sunrise or sunset.

eglisenotredamedumontcarmeldemahdia.d: The Catholic church in Mahdia, dating from the colonial era.
eglisenotredamedumontcarmeldemahdia.a: A Catholic church from the colonial era, bearing witness to Mahdia’s diverse past.
eglisenotredamedumontcarmeldemahdia.c: Opening hours vary: please check on site.

pharedemahdiacapafrique.d: Lighthouse at the tip of the Mahdia peninsula (Cap Afrique).
pharedemahdiacapafrique.a: Lighthouse at the tip of the peninsula (Cap Afrique), a maritime landmark offering views of the coastline.
pharedemahdiacapafrique.c: A lovely walk to the tip; access to the interior may be restricted.

pharedechebba.d: Chebba Lighthouse, near Cape Ras Kapoudia.
pharedechebba.a: Lighthouse near Cape Ras Kapoudia, on the rocky Sahel coastline.
pharedechebba.c: Coastal viewpoint: approach via the coast, as access to the lighthouse itself may be restricted.

grandchapiteaucorinthieneljem.d: A large ancient Corinthian capital amongst the Roman ruins of Thysdrus in El Jem.
grandchapiteaucorinthieneljem.a: Large ancient Corinthian capital amongst the scattered ruins of Thysdrus in El Jem.
grandchapiteaucorinthieneljem.c: A detail to look out for when visiting the Roman ruins at El Jem.

secondamphitheatredeljem.d: Ruins of a second Roman amphitheatre at Thysdrus, distinct from the main amphitheatre.
secondamphitheatredeljem.a: Levelled remains of a second amphitheatre at Thysdrus, older and far less well-preserved than the main amphitheatre.
secondamphitheatredeljem.c: Worth seeing as a complement to the main amphitheatre, for those who are curious.

henchirbirelmenadla.d: Ancient archaeological site (henchir) to the west of the Mahdia governorate, near the border with Kairouan.
henchirbirelmenadla.a: Ancient archaeological site (henchir) in the west of the Mahdia governorate; modest remains.
henchirbirelmenadla.c: Mainly of archaeological interest: check locally for access details.

atelierdepotierdesidibouzid.d: Ancient potter’s workshop listed as a historic monument, near the town of Sidi Bouzid.
atelierdepotierdesidibouzid.a: Ancient potter’s workshop listed as a historic monument, near the town of Sidi Bouzid.
atelierdepotierdesidibouzid.c: Specialised site: best visited with a guide to fully appreciate its significance.

henchirbouzer.d: Ruins (Henchir) in the north of the governorate of Sidi Bouzid.
henchirbouzer.a: Ancient ruins (henchir) in the north of the Sidi Bouzid governorate; rather unspectacular remains.

campdeconcentrationdemeherizebbeus.d: Former concentration camp established in 1939 in the Meknassy region.
campdeconcentrationdemeherizebbeus.a: Site of a camp established in 1939 in the Meknassy region; a place of remembrance.
campdeconcentrationdemeherizebbeus.c: A memorial site with no tourist facilities; enquire locally.

youngaiunca.d: Ancient Roman and Byzantine city south of Mahres, with Christian activity dating back to the 5th century.
youngaiunca.a: Roman and Byzantine city south of Mahres, characterised by Christian activity from the 5th century onwards.
youngaiunca.c: Extensive, largely undeveloped coastal site: bring water and sturdy footwear.

bordjelhassarkerkennah.d: Historic fort in the Kerkennah archipelago, near El Abbassia.
bordjelhassarkerkennah.a: A medieval fort with Spanish and Turkish influences on the Kerkennah archipelago, near El Abbassia.
bordjelhassarkerkennah.c: Best combined with a tour of the archipelago and its traditional fishing practices.

rouggabararus.d: The ancient Roman city of Bararus, approximately 13 km south-east of El Jem.
rouggabararus.a: The ancient Roman city of Bararus, about ten kilometres south-east of El Jem.
rouggabararus.c: A largely undeveloped rural site: a guide helps visitors to locate and interpret it.

amphitheatredebararus.d: Roman amphitheatre at the ancient site of Bararus (Rougga), south-east of El Jem.
amphitheatredebararus.a: Remains of a Roman amphitheatre at the Bararus (Rougga) site, south-east of El Jem.
amphitheatredebararus.c: Well worth visiting alongside the rest of the Rougga site, for lovers of antiquity.

kasrerressassacholla.d: Listed monument at the ancient site of Acholla.
kasrerressassacholla.a: Listed monument at the ancient site of Acholla, on the Sahel coast.
kasrerressassacholla.c: To be included in a visit to the Acholla site.

baptisteredesidimansour.d: Ancient baptistery near Sidi Mansour, north of Sfax.
baptisteredesidimansour.a: Ancient early Christian baptistery near Sidi Mansour, north of Sfax.
baptisteredesidimansour.c: A secluded site: ask locally for directions.

museearcheologiquedesfax.d: Archaeological Museum of the city of Sfax.
museearcheologiquedesfax.a: The city museum displays ancient collections from the region, including mosaics.
museearcheologiquedesfax.c: A good introduction before exploring the medina and the surrounding ancient sites.
museearcheologiquedesfax.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on arrival.

museedupatrimoineinsulairedekerkennah.d: Island Heritage Museum on the Kerkennah Archipelago.
museedupatrimoineinsulairedekerkennah.a: A museum dedicated to the heritage and traditions of the Kerkennah Archipelago, particularly fishing.
museedupatrimoineinsulairedekerkennah.c: Well worth a visit to gain an insight into island life before setting off to explore the islands.
museedupatrimoineinsulairedekerkennah.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on arrival.

eglisesaintpierreetsaintpauldesfax.a: A Catholic church dating from the colonial era, reflecting Sfax’s diverse heritage.
eglisesaintpierreetsaintpauldesfax.c: Opening times vary: please check on site.

mosqueesidiamarkammoun.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosqueesidiamarkammoun.a: Historic mosque in the Sfax medina.
mosqueesidiamarkammoun.c: Place of worship: view from the outside and keep a low profile.

mosqueesidielyessfax.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosqueesidielyessfax.a: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosqueesidielyessfax.c: Place of worship: view from the outside and be discreet.

mosqueesidiabdelmoula.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosqueesidiabdelmoula.a: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosqueesidiabdelmoula.c: Place of worship: view from the outside and be discreet.

mosqueeeltrouksfax.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosqueeeltrouksfax.a: Ottoman mosque in the medina of Sfax, a reminder of the Turkish era.
mosqueeeltrouksfax.c: Place of worship: view from the outside and remain discreet.

mosqueesidiellakhmi.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosqueesidiellakhmi.a: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosqueesidiellakhmi.c: Place of worship: view from the outside and remain discreet.

elabbassiakerkennah.d: A village in the Kerkennah Archipelago, near Bordj El Hassar Fort.
elabbassiakerkennah.a: A village in the Kerkennah Archipelago, near Bordj El Hassar Fort.
elabbassiakerkennah.c: A convenient starting point for visiting the nearby fort.

pharederasthyna.d: Lighthouse at Cape Ras Thyna, south of Sfax.
pharederasthyna.a: Lighthouse at Cape Ras Thyna, south of Sfax, near the ancient site of Thaenae.
pharederasthyna.c: Coastal landmark to be approached from the coast; to be used in conjunction with the site of Thyna.

pharedelilecharkikerkennah.d: Lighthouse on Charki Island (Kerkennah), at the entrance to the Sfax channel.
pharedelilecharkikerkennah.a: The lighthouse on Charki Island, at the entrance to the Sfax channel, in the Kerkennah archipelago.
pharedelilecharkikerkennah.c: Visible during a boat trip around the archipelago.

campdeconcentrationdetnietagareb.d: Former Second World War concentration camp near Agareb.
campdeconcentrationdetnietagareb.a: Site of a Second World War camp near Agareb; a place of remembrance.
campdeconcentrationdetnietagareb.c: A memorial site with no tourist facilities; please enquire locally.

naraggarasakietsidiyoussef.d: The ancient city of Africa Proconsularis, mentioned by Livy near Scipio’s camp prior to the Battle of Zama (202 BC). Corresponds to Sakiet Sidi Youssef, near the Algerian border.
naraggarasakietsidiyoussef.a: The remains of the ancient city mentioned by Livy near Scipio’s camp before Zama, at Sakiet Sidi Youssef.
naraggarasakietsidiyoussef.c: Near the Algerian border: mainly of historical interest; check for information on access to the border area.

tajerouine.d: A town in the Kef Governorate, approximately 38 km south-west of Kef, at the foot of Djebel Slata.
tajerouine.a: A stopover town at the foot of Djebel Slata, a starting point for exploring the surrounding sites.
tajerouine.c: More of a stopover than a destination: useful for exploring the south-west of El Kef.

dahmaniebbaksour.d: A town in the Kef governorate, formerly known as Ebba Ksour, close to the ancient site of Althiburos.
dahmaniebbaksour.a: A town (formerly Ebba Ksour) serving as a gateway to the nearby ancient site of Althiburos.
dahmaniebbaksour.c: Make it your base for visiting nearby Althiburos.

lesers.d: A town about 35 km south-east of El Kef, in a grain-growing region.
lesers.a: A town in a grain-growing region, with no major monuments, on the plain to the south-east of El Kef.
lesers.c: A simple stop-off on the road; of little tourist interest in its own right.

nebeur.d: A town in the Kef governorate, near the Mellegue Dam.
nebeur.a: A village near the Mellegue Dam and its wadi landscapes.
nebeur.c: Combine with a visit to the nearby Mellegue Dam.

touiref.d: A town in the north of the Kef governorate.
touiref.a: A village in the north of Kef, near the ruins of Masculula.
touiref.c: A possible starting point for a trip to the ancient site of Masculula.

jerissa.d: A town in the Kef governorate, known for its iron mine and the Amazigh, Punic and Roman ruins in the surrounding area.
jerissa.a: A mining town (iron) surrounded by Amazigh, Punic and Roman ruins.
jerissa.c: A stop for those interested in mining heritage and the ruins scattered around the area.

kalaatessenam.d: A town in the west of the Kef governorate, at the foot of the Table de Jugurtha.
kalaatessenam.a: A town at the foot of the spectacular Table de Jugurtha, the starting point for the ascent.
kalaatessenam.c: An ideal base before climbing the Table de Jugurtha: set off in the morning and take plenty of water with you.

elksourlekef.d: A town and municipality in the Kef Governorate.
elksourlekef.a: A small town and municipality in the Kef Governorate, with no major monuments.
elksourlekef.c: A simple stopover in the region.

mascululahenchirguergour.d: The ruins of ancient Masculula near Touiref, where Neo-Punic and Latin inscriptions were discovered (some of which are in the Louvre).
mascululahenchirguergour.a: The ruins of ancient Masculula, where Neo-Punic and Latin inscriptions were found (some of which are in the Louvre).
mascululahenchirguergour.c: A rural site near Touiref, largely undeveloped: best left to epigraphy enthusiasts with the exact coordinates.

silianaville.d: Capital of the governorate of Siliana, on the western edge of the Tunisian mountain range.
silianaville.a: The governorate capital, a starting point for visits to ancient sites and the mountains of the Tunisian mountain range.
silianaville.c: A good logistical base from which to explore Makthar, Ksar Lemsa and Djebel Serj.

bouarada.d: A town in the north of the Siliana governorate, at the foot of Djebel Bargou.
bouarada.a: A town at the foot of Djebel Bargou, close to the ancient site of Apisa Maius.
bouarada.c: A stopover on the way to Djebel Bargou and the ruins of Apisa Maius.

gaafour.d: A town in the governorate of Siliana, on the north-western railway line.
gaafour.a: A stopover town on the north-western railway line.
gaafour.c: Primarily a transport hub; of little tourist interest in its own right.

bargou.d: A town nestled against the northern slope of Djebel Bargou (Siliana).
bargou.a: A village nestled against the northern slope of Djebel Bargou, in a lush mountainous setting.
bargou.c: A starting point for hikes on Jebel Bargou; pleasant in spring.

rouhia.d: A town in the south of the governorate of Siliana, in the highland grain-growing region.
rouhia.a: A town in the cereal-growing highlands of southern Siliana.
rouhia.c: A simple stopover in an agricultural area.

elkrib.d: A town in the north of the Siliana governorate, close to the ancient site of Musti.
elkrib.a: A modern town adjacent to the ancient site of Musti, with its Arch of Gordian III and its macellum.
elkrib.c: Park at El Krib to visit Musti on foot, which is right next door.

thacia.d: A city from Roman Africa and a former bishopric, the ruins of which are situated near El Krib (Siliana).
thacia.a: The ruins of a Roman city and former bishopric, near El Krib.
thacia.c: Best visited in combination with the neighbouring Musti and El Krib; a modest site best located using coordinates.

apisamaius.d: Ancient city of Proconsular Africa and episcopal see (Tarf ech Chenah), near Bou Arada.
apisamaius.a: The remains of a city in Proconsular Africa and a former episcopal see (Tarf ech Chenah).
apisamaius.c: Near Bou Arada; an unassuming rural site, particularly for archaeology enthusiasts.

kasserineville.d: Capital of the governorate of Kasserine, at the foot of Djebel Chambi, on the site of ancient Cillium.
kasserineville.a: The capital at the foot of Djebel Chambi, built on the site of ancient Cillium and the gateway to the national park.
kasserineville.c: A base for exploring Djebel Chambi and the sites of Cillium and the Mausoleum of the Flavii.

feriana.d: A town in the south-west of the governorate of Kasserine, close to the ancient site of Thelepte.
feriana.a: A town near the extensive ancient site of Thelepte.
feriana.c: Make this your starting point for visiting Thelepte, some 5 km away.

foussana.d: A town in the north-west of the Kasserine governorate, near the Algerian border.
foussana.a: A town in the north-west of Kasserine, between Djebel Bireno and the Algerian border.
foussana.c: A stop-off on the way to Djebel Bireno; check access to this mountainous border area.

sbibaville.d: A town in the governorate of Kasserine, situated on the site of ancient Sufes (where the basilica has been converted into a mosque).
sbibaville.a: The town stands on the site of ancient Sufes, whose basilica has been converted into a mosque.
sbibaville.c: Look out for the ruins of Sufes scattered throughout the town; a short visit.

thalaville.d: A town in the governorate of Kasserine, at an altitude of around 1,017 metres, one of the highest and coldest in Tunisia.
thalaville.a: A high-altitude town (~1,017 m) that has retained its ancient name, one of the highest and coldest in Tunisia.
thalaville.c: Wrap up warm; combine this with a visit to the archaeological site of Thala.

hassielferid.d: A town and sub-prefecture in the south-west of the Kasserine governorate.
hassielferid.a: A small sub-prefecture town in the south-west of Kasserine, with no major sites.

elayoun.d: A town and sub-prefecture in the north of the Kasserine governorate.
elayoun.a: A town in the north of the Kasserine governorate, with no notable monuments.

jedelienne.d: A town and sub-prefecture in the north-east of the governorate of Kasserine.
jedelienne.a: A town in the north-east of Kasserine.

magelbelabbes.d: A town in the far south-west of the Kasserine governorate, near the Algerian border.
magelbelabbes.a: A town in the far south-west of Kasserine, near the Algerian border.
magelbelabbes.c: Border area: check access details before travelling there.

museearcheologiquedesbeitla.d: Museum in Sbeitla, opposite the archaeological site, featuring mosaics and artefacts from prehistoric times to the Islamic period.
museearcheologiquedesbeitla.a: Mosaics and artefacts dating from prehistoric times to the Islamic period, opposite the Sufetula site.
museearcheologiquedesbeitla.c: A short visit (~45 mins) to combine with the archaeological site directly opposite.
museearcheologiquedesbeitla.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on arrival.

babsouika.d: A square and working-class neighbourhood to the north of the medina, the heart of the city’s festive life: cafés with live music, the Sulâmiyya Sufi ensemble, Ramadan evenings (‘Layali Bab Souika’). The original gate, demolished in 1861, gave the place its name.
babsouika.a: Nearby: the Youssef Saheb Ettabaa Mosque (1814), with its precious marble; the atmosphere of the singing cafés and evening events.
babsouika.c: L livelier in the evenings and during the festive season; a good starting point for a walk to Halfaouine.

babmenara.d: A neighbourhood on the south-western side of the medina, near Zitouna University, named after a former gate in the city walls that no longer exists.
babmenara.a: Nearby: Dar Othman, a sumptuous late 16th-century palace (Othman Dey), renowned for its façade.
babmenara.c: Simply a landmark marking the entrance to the Upper Medina; worth a quick visit.

babbnet.d: A neighbourhood in the western part of the medina, near the administrative kasbah, which takes its name from one of the oldest gates (built around 1228–1249), which no longer exists. The name now refers to the neighbourhood itself.
babbnet.a: Nearby: the Collège Sadiki (1875), the cradle of Tunisian modernity, which overlooks the medina with its minaret and domes.
babbnet.c: Well worth a look as you make your way from Kasbah Square to the medina.

babelfellah.d: A neighbourhood to the south of the medina, named after a gate that disappeared around 1890 and which opened onto the southern suburbs (cemeteries and zaouias). The gate no longer exists; the name remains for the neighbourhood.
babelfellah.a: The neighbourhood leads to the mosque and mausoleum of Sidi Béchir Ziri, founder of a Rahmania zaouïa.
babelfellah.c: A quick stop on the southern edge of the medina.

babalioua.d: The south-eastern gate of the medina of Tunis, the historic starting point for the routes to the Sahel and the south.
babalioua.a: The south-eastern gate of the medina, the historic starting point for the routes to the Sahel and the south of the country, now situated in a very busy transport hub.
babalioua.c: A busy crossroads: simply a landmark, with no interior to visit.

babelallouj.d: Former gate in the walls of the Tunis medina, on the north-western side, near the kasbah.
babelallouj.a: The former gate on the north-western side of the walls, near the Kasbah, a remnant of the medina’s gate system.
babelallouj.c: A brief stop to be combined with visits to the other gates in the Kasbah area.

palaissahebettabaa.d: The Beylical palace in the Halfaouine district, associated with the dignitary Saheb Ettabaa, early 19th century.
palaissahebettabaa.a: The ornate reception rooms and courtyard of the former Beylical Palace of the dignitary Saheb Ettabaa in the Halfaouine district.
palaissahebettabaa.c: Best visited in conjunction with the Saheb Ettabaa Mosque and the bustling Halfaouine square.

darothman.d: Othman Dey’s Palace in the medina of Tunis, with its polychrome marble façade, one of the city’s oldest palaces.
darothman.a: The polychrome marble façade and ornate gateway of one of the oldest palaces in the medina, with its inner courtyard and garden.
darothman.c: A little gem of residential architecture; a short visit to the heart of the medina.

darelbeypalaisdugouvernement.d: Former Beylical palace in the Kasbah of Tunis, now the seat of the Presidency of the Government.
darelbeypalaisdugouvernement.a: The imposing façade of the former Beylical palace in the Kasbah, now the seat of the Presidency of the Government, on Kasbah Square.
darelbeypalaisdugouvernement.c: An official building not open to the public: best viewed from the square, alongside the neighbouring Kasbah Mosque.

grandesynagoguedetunis.d: Tunis’s main synagogue, built in the late 1930s in the modern part of the city in the Art Deco style.
grandesynagoguedetunis.a: The Art Deco façade of the capital’s main synagogue, built in the modern part of the city in the late 1930s, on Avenue de la Liberté.
grandesynagoguedetunis.c: Access is restricted and secured: please enquire in advance if you wish to visit.

eglisesaintjosephdetunis.d: A Catholic church in the modern part of Tunis, built during the Protectorate era.
eglisesaintjosephdetunis.a: The Catholic church dating from the Protectorate era and its interior, in the modern part of Tunis.
eglisesaintjosephdetunis.c: Well worth a look whilst strolling through the colonial city centre.

eglisesaintejeannedarcdetunis.d: Catholic church in the northern district of Tunis (Lafayette), featuring colonial-era architecture.
eglisesaintejeannedarcdetunis.a: The colonial-era architecture of this church in the northern district (Lafayette) of modern Tunis.
eglisesaintejeannedarcdetunis.c: Of architectural interest above all; a brief stop in the modern city centre.

museenationaldartmoderneetcontemporainde.d: Museum of Modern and Contemporary Tunisian Art, in the Cité de la Culture in Tunis.
museenationaldartmoderneetcontemporainde.a: The collections of modern and contemporary Tunisian paintings and sculptures, on display at the Cité de la Culture.
museenationaldartmoderneetcontemporainde.c: A contemporary complement to the Bardo; check the opening days of the Cité de la Culture.
museenationaldartmoderneetcontemporainde.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

palaisdeksarsaid.d: 19th-century Beylical Palace near the Bardo, where the Treaty of the Bardo (1881) was signed.
palaisdeksarsaid.a: The 19th-century Beylical Palace, with its ornate salons and the historic setting where the Treaty of Bardo of 1881 was signed, near the Bardo.
palaisdeksarsaid.c: Best combined with a visit to the neighbouring Bardo Museum; check opening times following restoration work.

museepaleochretiendecarthage.d: Site museum showcasing the early Christian remains of Carthage.
museepaleochretiendecarthage.a: Early Christian remains and artefacts (sarcophagi, mosaics, architectural elements) displayed in a site museum in the heart of Carthage.
museepaleochretiendecarthage.c: A short themed stop to include in your tour of Carthage.
museepaleochretiendecarthage.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

quartierhannibalcarthage.d: Remains of a Punic residential quarter on the southern slope of Byrsa, illustrating the urban layout of Carthage prior to 146 BC.
quartierhannibalcarthage.a: The streets and foundations of Punic dwellings unearthed on the southern slope of Byrsa, bearing witness to the urban layout of Carthage prior to 146 BC.
quartierhannibalcarthage.c: Well worth a visit immediately after the Byrsa Museum to understand the original Punic city.

edificeacolonnesdecarthage.d: Roman colonnaded monument in the archaeological area of Carthage, near the Roman villas.
edificeacolonnesdecarthage.a: The Roman colonnaded monument in the archaeological site, near the villas on the Odeon Hill.
edificeacolonnesdecarthage.c: A modest ruin to include in a walk around the Roman villas.

synagoguebeitmordekhaidelagoulette.d: The synagogue at La Goulette, a testament to the Jewish community of the port of Tunis.
synagoguebeitmordekhaidelagoulette.a: The synagogue at La Goulette, a testament to the port’s former Jewish community and its cosmopolitan past.
synagoguebeitmordekhaidelagoulette.c: Access may be restricted; worth seeing whilst strolling through the La Goulette neighbourhood.

kalaatelandalous.d: A village founded by the Andalusians (Moriscos) in the 17th century, on a promontory overlooking the lower Medjerda and Lake Ghar El Melh.
kalaatelandalous.a: The Morisco village perched on its promontory, with its ancient alleyways and panoramic views of the lower Medjerda and the Ghar El Melh lagoon.
kalaatelandalous.c: A beautiful viewpoint in the morning or evening light; well worth combining with a visit to the nearby mouth of the Medjerda.

palaisborjbaccoucheariana.d: The former Ariana Bey’s residence, an example of the holiday architecture favoured by Tunisian dignitaries.
palaisborjbaccoucheariana.a: The former Ariana summer residence of the Bey and its architecture, typical of the country estates of Tunisian dignitaries.
palaisborjbaccoucheariana.c: A modest site, sometimes with limited access; a brief stop for enthusiasts of Beylical heritage.

harasnationaldesidithabet.d: The historic Sidi Thabet horse breeding centre (Barb and Arab-Barb horses).
harasnationaldesidithabet.a: The historic horse breeding centre specialising in Barb and Arab-Barb horses, its stables and its thoroughbreds.
harasnationaldesidithabet.c: Of interest to horse enthusiasts; check the visiting conditions and opening hours.

palaiskobbetelnhasmanouba.d: The palatial pavilion with its copper dome in Manouba, a remnant of the Beylical summer residences.
palaiskobbetelnhasmanouba.a: The palatial pavilion crowned with its characteristic copper dome, a remnant of the Beylical summer residences on the Manouba plain.
palaiskobbetelnhasmanouba.c: A small, isolated monument best viewed from the outside whilst passing through Manouba.

palaismouradbeymanouba.d: Former Beylical palace in Manouba associated with the Mouradids, a holiday resort area to the west of Tunis.
palaismouradbeymanouba.a: The remains of the former Beylical palace associated with the Mouradids, a testament to the holiday resorts to the west of Tunis.
palaismouradbeymanouba.c: A modest site; best visited in conjunction with the other Beylical residences in the Manouba region.

tebourbathuburbominus.d: A town in the Medjerda Valley on the site of ancient Thuburbo Minus (a Roman colony), repopulated by Andalusians in the 17th century.
tebourbathuburbominus.a: The old Andalusian town in the Medjerda Valley and the remains of ancient Thuburbo Minus, including the ruins of the amphitheatre.
tebourbathuburbominus.c: A countryside stop in the Medjerda Valley; combine with a visit to the amphitheatre and the Sidi Ali Azouz mausoleum.

amphitheatredetebourba.d: Remains of the Roman amphitheatre of ancient Thuburbo Minus, in Tebourba.
amphitheatredetebourba.a: The levelled remains of the Roman amphitheatre of ancient Thuburbo Minus, set within the modern town; a modest site.
amphitheatredetebourba.c: A quick visit to include as part of a stroll through Tebourba.

mausoleesidialiazouztebourba.d: Zaouïa and mausoleum of a Sufi saint in Tebourba, in the heart of the old town.
mausoleesidialiazouztebourba.a: The zaouïa and mausoleum of the Sufi saint, with its traditional décor, in the heart of Tebourba’s old town.
mausoleesidialiazouztebourba.c: Appropriate attire is required; a brief spiritual stop in the old town centre.

pontbarragedelbatan.d: An ancient hydraulic structure on the Medjerda at El Batan, linked to the fulling mills of the valley.
pontbarragedelbatan.a: The ancient waterworks on the Medjerda and the remains of the fulling mills that made the valley’s reputation for textiles.
pontbarragedelbatan.c: An interesting example of historic industrial heritage, well worth seeing on a tour of the Medjerda Valley.

cimetieremilitairedemassicaultborjelamri.d: Commonwealth War Graves Cemetery (soldiers from the 1943 Tunisian campaign).
cimetieremilitairedemassicaultborjelamri.a: The neat rows of headstones in the Commonwealth cemetery, set in well-maintained grounds, where soldiers from the 1943 Tunisian campaign are laid to rest.
cimetieremilitairedemassicaultborjelamri.c: A well-maintained place of remembrance; a sombre visit, best combined with a trip to the Medjerda Valley.

palaisdelamohammedia.d: Ruins of the Beylical Palace of Ahmed I Bey (mid-19th century) in La Mohammedia, nicknamed the ‘Tunisian Versailles’, which remains unfinished.
palaisdelamohammedia.a: The romantic ruins of the unfinished palace of Ahmed I Bey, nicknamed the ‘Tunisian Versailles’, whose arcades and sections of wall still stand on the plain.
palaisdelamohammedia.c: An evocative, derelict site; wear sturdy shoes and take care whilst walking amongst the ruins.

thermesdoudhnauthina.d: The great public baths of the Roman colony of Uthina (Oudhna), south of Tunis.
thermesdoudhnauthina.a: The grand public baths of the Roman colony of Uthina, with their rooms and substructures, in the archaeological area of Oudhna.
thermesdoudhnauthina.c: Worth seeing as part of a general tour of the Oudhna site.

cimetieremilitaireallemanddeborjcedria.d: German military necropolis for soldiers of the Second World War, with graves in Tunisia, on the heights of Borj Cedria.
