cimetieremilitaireallemanddeborjcedria.a: The German military necropolis from the Second World War, with its massive crypt and graves clustered on the heights overlooking the gulf.
cimetieremilitaireallemanddeborjcedria.c: An austere memorial site offering a view of the coast; a brief and sombre visit.

aqueducdezaghouanacarthage.d: A Roman aqueduct stretching over 130 km, carrying water from the springs of Zaghouan to Carthage; long rows of arches are still visible. Coordinates of a section.
aqueducdezaghouanacarthage.a: The long rows of Roman arches still standing in the plain, remnants of the more than 130 km of aqueduct that carried water from Zaghouan to Carthage.
aqueducdezaghouanacarthage.c: The arches are clearly visible from the Tunis–Zaghouan road, particularly towards Mohammedia/Oudhna; beautiful low-angle light at the end of the day.

thermesromainsdedjebeloust.d: A Roman thermal bath complex built around a hot spring at Djebel Oust (mosaics), later converted into an early Christian complex.
thermesromainsdedjebeloust.a: The thermal baths surrounding the hot spring, with their mosaics still in place, and the early Christian structures that succeeded them.
thermesromainsdedjebeloust.c: A specialist site with few visitors; check for access details; best combined with a visit to Zaghouan.

grandemosqueedezaghouan.d: The Hanafi mosque in the town of Zaghouan, set within the historic town centre at the foot of the djebel.
grandemosqueedezaghouan.a: The Hanafi mosque and its minaret in the old town, at the foot of the djebel.
grandemosqueedezaghouan.c: Well worth seeing whilst strolling through the medina of Zaghouan and its fountains.

arcromaindezaghouan.d: A triumphal arch / Roman gate still standing in the town of Zaghouan, at the foot of the Temple of the Waters.
arcromaindezaghouan.a: The Roman arch (monumental gate) still standing in the town, at the foot of the path leading up to the Temple of the Waters.
arcromaindezaghouan.c: A stop on the way to the Temple of the Waters; a short break.

abthugnihenchiressouar.d: Roman city in the south of the Zaghouan governorate, featuring a forum, a temple and municipal ruins.
abthugnihenchiressouar.a: The remains of the forum, a temple and municipal features of the Roman city, scattered across the countryside in the south of the governorate.
abthugnihenchiressouar.c: A modest site with few facilities for enthusiasts; a vehicle is essential and local guidance is recommended.

abbirmaius.d: Ancient Roman city in the El Fahs region (Zaghouan), known for its inscriptions and ruins.
abbirmaius.a: The scattered remains of the ancient Roman city in the El Fahs region, known primarily for its inscriptions.
abbirmaius.c: A site in a state of advanced ruin, best suited to enthusiasts of epigraphy and archaeology; a local guide is recommended.

segermeshenchirharat.d: Site of the ancient Roman city of Segermes, to the east of the governorate of Zaghouan, the subject of Danish-Tunisian excavations.
segermeshenchirharat.a: The remains of the ancient Roman city of Segermes, unearthed by Danish-Tunisian excavations, to the east of the governorate.
segermeshenchirharat.c: A site of scientific interest with few signposts; check locally before visiting.

eglisesaintehelenedezaghouan.d: Former Catholic church in the town of Zaghouan, a reminder of the Protectorate period.
eglisesaintehelenedezaghouan.a: The former Catholic church from the Protectorate period in the town of Zaghouan, a fine example of colonial architecture.
eglisesaintehelenedezaghouan.c: A small heritage site worth seeing whilst passing through Zaghouan.

arcdegordieniiimustielkrib.d: Monumental arch of ancient Musti (El Krib), dated 239 according to an inscription, marking one of the eastern entrances to the city (a ceremonial gate rather than a triumphal arch). Coordinates within the site are approximate.
arcdegordieniiimustielkrib.a: A monumental arch dating from 239, marking an eastern entrance to ancient Musti.
arcdegordieniiimustielkrib.c: Highlight of the Musti site; a quick visit whilst walking around the site.

marcheromainmacellumdemustielkrib.d: Covered market (macellum) of ancient Musti, built of white limestone, at the heart of the site alongside the forum, temples and cisterns. Coordinates within the site are approximate.
marcheromainmacellumdemustielkrib.a: An ancient covered market made of white limestone, situated at the heart of the site alongside the forum, temples and cisterns.
marcheromainmacellumdemustielkrib.c: Worth seeing whilst exploring Musti; this particular spot can be viewed in just a few minutes.

fortsantiagoborjchikly.d: A fort stands on the islet of Chikly, in the middle of Lake Tunis. A former citadel of Roman origin, rebuilt by the Spanish governor of La Goulette between 1546 and 1550 (Santiago de Chikly). Listed as a national cultural heritage site in 1993.
fortsantiagoborjchikly.a: The Hispano-Ottoman fort on the islet of Chikly in the middle of the lake, rebuilt in the 16th century on older foundations, within the bird sanctuary.
fortsantiagoborjchikly.c: Access to the islet is restricted (permit required, boat crossing): please check with the INP before visiting.

citernesdebordjdjedidcarthage.d: A vast complex of Roman cisterns on the hill of Bordj Djedid in Carthage, near the shore, distinct from the cisterns at La Malga. Supplied by a vaulted aqueduct. Approximate coordinates.
citernesdebordjdjedidcarthage.a: The extensive complex of vaulted Roman cisterns near the shore, distinct from those at La Malga, which contributed to Carthage’s water supply.
citernesdebordjdjedidcarthage.c: An unassuming hydraulic monument to be included in the seaside tour of Carthage.

hotelsididrissdecorstarwarsfermedeslars.d: The cave hotel in Matmata, whose inner courtyard served as the setting for the interior of the Lars’ farm (Luke Skywalker’s home) in Star Wars IV: A New Hope (1977), and was reused for Episodes II (2002) and III (2005). Distinct from the centre of Matmata.
hotelsididrissdecorstarwarsfermedeslars.a: A cave hotel in Matmata, whose courtyard served as the interior of the Lars’ farm in Star Wars (1977, then 2002 and 2005).
hotelsididrissdecorstarwarsfermedeslars.c: The site is still in use: visitors can enjoy a cup of tea or stay overnight to see the set; it gets busy at peak times.

fermedeslarsdomechotteldjeridpresdenefta.d: The exterior set of the Lars’ farm (the dome/igloo), built on the Chott el-Djerid to the west of Nefta for Star Wars IV (1977), and rebuilt for Episodes II and III. Distinct from Tozeur and Nefta.
fermedeslarsdomechotteldjeridpresdenefta.a: Exterior set of the Lars’ farm (the dome) built on the Chott el-Djerid, west of Nefta, for Star Wars.
fermedeslarsdomechotteldjeridpresdenefta.c: Access via the track across the chott: a 4x4 is recommended, and do come early in the morning to enjoy the light and the cool air.

babelbharportedefrance.d: A historic gate marking the boundary between the medina of Tunis and the European quarter, nicknamed the ‘Gate of France’. The arch has stood alone since the demolition of the city walls.
babelbharportedefrance.a: The monumental arch marking the entrance to the medina of Tunis, the dividing line between the Arab quarter and the European quarter.
babelbharportedefrance.c: A central landmark and the ideal starting point for a tour of the medina from Avenue Bourguiba.

tourbetelbey.d: The royal necropolis of the Husaynid dynasty, built in the 18th century. Beneath its domes lie beys, princes and ministers. The interior boasts sumptuous décor — polychrome faience, carved marble and chiselled stucco — blending Italian, Andalusian and Ottoman influences. The men’s tombs are topped with a stele bearing a chechia, whilst those of the women remain unadorned.
tourbetelbey.a: The décor of faience and marble; the striking contrast between the unassuming alleyway and the opulence of the interior.
tourbetelbey.c: Often overlooked by visitors: a peaceful haven to the south of the medina. Best visited in conjunction with the neighbouring Dar Ben Abdallah.

medersaslimania.d: A Koranic school founded in 1754 by Ali I Pasha in memory of his son Slimane. Situated very close to the Zitouna, on Rue des Libraires, it is organised around a porticoed courtyard with black-and-white painted arches, flanked by the cells where the students lived.
medersaslimania.a: The courtyard with its two-tone arches; the row of three madrasas on Rue des Libraires.
medersaslimania.c: On the way between the Zitouna and the souks. Check opening times on arrival.

darbenabdallah.d: An aristocratic palace dating from the late 18th century, now the Museum of Folk Arts and Traditions of Tunis. Surrounding a marble courtyard with a fountain, the richly decorated rooms — with painted wooden ceilings, chiselled stucco and faience — recreate the lifestyle of Tunis’s leading families: wedding scenes, costumes and ceremonial furniture.
darbenabdallah.a: The columned courtyard with its fountain; the rooms recreating domestic life of yesteryear.
darbenabdallah.c: The best place to gain an insight into the interior of a dar (patio house). Situated next to the Tourbet El Bey.

placedelakasbah.d: A vast administrative square to the west of the medina, the heart of Tunisian power: the Prime Minister’s Office (Dar El Bey) and government buildings, the Kasbah Mosque and its Almohad minaret. The official buildings are not open to visitors, but the complex as a whole — square, palace and mosque — is well worth a look.
placedelakasbah.a: The Almohad minaret of the Kasbah Mosque; the harmony of the official square; the view towards the Upper Medina.
placedelakasbah.c: Not open to visitors (seat of government), but very photogenic from the outside. A natural gateway to the Upper Medina.

babelassel.d: A neighbourhood in the northern part of the medina (Bab Souika area), centred around an ancient gate. Its name is thought to derive from the Bani Assal family who lived there – or from the word for honey (‘assel’): the nearby ‘Rue du Miel’ (Honey Street) bears witness to this. The gate is also known as Bab Sidi Yahya, named after the neighbouring El Borj (Sidi Yahia) Mosque.
babelassel.a: The El Borj (Sidi Yahia) Mosque; the picturesque ‘Rue du Miel’.
babelassel.c: In the heart of the working-class northern part of the medina, on the way to Bab Souika and Halfaouine.

placehalfaouine.d: A lively square in the northern part of the medina, bustling with two souks (El Halfaouine and El Jedid). On the edge of the square stands the Youssef Saheb Ettabaa Mosque (1814). Its hammam inspired the cult film ‘Halfaouine, l’enfant des terrasses’ (Férid Boughedir, 1990, winner of the Tanit d’Or at the JCC), which brought the neighbourhood’s atmosphere to the attention of the whole world.
placehalfaouine.a: The bustling square and its souks; the nearby Saheb Ettabaa Mosque; the hammam made famous by the film.
placehalfaouine.c: The heart of the working-class north – take a stroll, have a coffee. More authentic and less touristy than the centre.

hafsia.d: The former Jewish quarter of the medina (the ‘hara’), where Jews were welcomed as early as the 10th century by Sidi Mahrez. Having fallen into poverty and then been partially demolished, it was restored in the 1970s and 1980s by the Association for the Preservation of the Medina — an award-winning project that has become a textbook example of urban planning. Today, it is home to the famous second-hand clothes market.
hafsia.a: The second-hand clothes market; the restored architecture blending the old with the rebuilt; the legacy of the Jewish quarter.
hafsia.c: A place to hunt for bargains and get a feel for today’s working-class Tunis. Haggling is a must.

parcnationaldelichkeul.d: The national park around Lake Ichkeul and its wetlands, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a Ramsar site. A major stopover for migratory birds.
parcnationaldelichkeul.a: The lake and its wetlands; herds of buffalo; the eco-museum and the trail to the thermal springs at the foot of the djebel; flocks of migratory birds.
parcnationaldelichkeul.c: Visit in winter to see waterbirds (coots, geese, flamingos); binoculars recommended.

lacichkeul.d: A brackish lake connected to the Bizerte lagoon, at the heart of Ichkeul National Park. A Ramsar site and UNESCO World Heritage Site.
lacichkeul.a: National Park (UNESCO, Ramsar): walking trails, an ecological museum, and above all the birdlife — flamingos, storks, pelicans, and thousands of coots and ducks overwintering here (229 animal species recorded). At the foot of the djebel (511 m), there are hot springs and traditional hammams, with Roman ruins nearby.
lacichkeul.c: Visit early in the morning or late in the afternoon (to avoid the heat); the best time for birdwatching is from October to February. Access to the national park is regulated: check with the forestry authorities (Eaux & Forêts / DGF).

parcnationaldedjebelchambi.d: National park home to Djebel Chambi, Tunisia’s highest peak (1,544 m). A biosphere reserve covering an Aleppo pine forest.
parcnationaldedjebelchambi.a: Tunisia’s highest peak (1,544 m) is situated within an Aleppo pine forest designated as a biosphere reserve, home to mountain wildlife.
parcnationaldedjebelchambi.c: Access is restricted: check for permits and safety requirements, and allow a full day and plenty of water for the hike.

parcnationaldebouhedma.d: A pre-Saharan steppe national park and biosphere reserve. A site for the reintroduction of antelopes and home to North Africa’s last acacia savannah.
parcnationaldebouhedma.a: A pre-Saharan steppe park and biosphere reserve, home to North Africa’s last acacia savannah and reintroduced antelopes.
parcnationaldebouhedma.c: Restricted access: check with the park authorities before visiting.

parcnationaldejbil.d: A Saharan national park situated in the Grand Erg Oriental, the largest in Tunisia. A reserve home to gazelles and addax.
parcnationaldejbil.a: Tunisia’s largest national park, in the heart of the Grand Erg Oriental, a refuge for gazelles and addax.
parcnationaldejbil.c: Deep desert: access by 4x4 with an authorised guide; water supplies are compulsory.

parcnationaldeboukornine.d: National park on Djebel Boukornine, a twin-peaked mountain overlooking the Gulf of Tunis near Hammam Lif. Rich Mediterranean flora.
parcnationaldeboukornine.a: Trails through the Mediterranean forest, the flora (cyclamen, irises) and viewpoints overlooking the Gulf of Tunis from the twin-peaked mountain.
parcnationaldeboukornine.c: Ideal in spring for the flora; walking boots, water, and departure from Hammam Lif.

parcnationaldelfeija.d: Kroumirie National Park, set amongst forests of cork oaks and Zeen oaks. A refuge for the Barbary deer. Approximate coordinates.
parcnationaldelfeija.a: The Kroumirie forest of cork oaks and zeen oaks, a refuge for the Barbary deer.
parcnationaldelfeija.c: Best visited in spring or autumn for the forest and wildlife; allow for travel by vehicle and walking, and observe the deer at dawn or dusk.

parcnationaldedghoumes.d: National park on the edge of Chott el-Jerid, at the foot of the djebel. A reserve for pre-Saharan steppe and wildlife reintroduction.
parcnationaldedghoumes.a: A pre-Saharan steppe park on the edge of Chott el-Jerid, dedicated to wildlife reintroduction.
parcnationaldedghoumes.c: Wildlife spotting is best early in the morning; find out about access arrangements.

parcnationaldesiditoui.d: A desert steppe national park in south-eastern Tunisia, near the Libyan border. A reserve for the rehabilitation of Saharan wildlife.
parcnationaldesiditoui.a: A desert steppe park in the south-east, dedicated to the rehabilitation of Saharan wildlife.
parcnationaldesiditoui.c: Remote area near the border: a guide and 4x4 are recommended.

parcnationaldejebelorbata.d: A mountain national park in the Gafsa region, featuring gorges and springs. Flora transitional between the Mediterranean and Saharan zones.
parcnationaldejebelorbata.a: A mountain park near Gafsa, featuring gorges, springs and flora transitional between the Mediterranean and Saharan zones.
parcnationaldejebelorbata.c: Hiking in rugged terrain: sturdy footwear, water and an early start are essential.

parcnationaldejebelserj.d: Tunisian Mountain Range National Park, comprising the Ain Soltane cave and forests of Aleppo pine and holm oak.
parcnationaldejebelserj.a: The Ain Soltane Cave and forests of Aleppo pine and holm oak on the Tunisian Ridge.
parcnationaldejebelserj.c: A lovely springtime nature walk; make sure you bring good walking shoes and water.

parcnationaldejebelzaghouan.d: A national park protecting Mount Zaghouan (1,295 m) and the Temple of the Waters, which supplied Carthage with water. The limestone massif of the Tunisian Ridge.
parcnationaldejebelzaghouan.a: The trails through the limestone massif, with views over the plain and the Temple of the Waters nestled at its foot.
parcnationaldejebelzaghouan.c: A cool hike at altitude; make sure you have good walking shoes and plenty of water, and combine it with a visit to the Temple of the Waters.

djebelzaghouan.d: A limestone peak rising to 1,295 m, one of the highest in north-eastern Tunisia. It overlooks the Zaghouan plain.
djebelzaghouan.a: The limestone summit overlooking the plain (1,295 m) and its sweeping panoramic views of north-eastern Tunisia from the ridges.
djebelzaghouan.c: A climb for experienced walkers; set off early, take water and a windbreaker; clear views on a clear day.

iledezembra.d: A mountainous island off the coast of Cap Bon, at the heart of the Zembra and Zembretta Islands National Park and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
iledezembra.a: The island’s cliffs and terrain; its rich marine life and bird colonies; the setting of the national park off Cap Bon.
iledezembra.c: A protected reserve with restricted access: best reached by boat trip.

parcnationaldesilesdezembraetzembretta.d: Marine and Island National Park off Cap Bon, a UNESCO biosphere reserve. An important seabird breeding site. Approximate coordinates.
parcnationaldesilesdezembraetzembretta.a: Marine and Island Park off Cap Bon, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and an important seabird breeding site.
parcnationaldesilesdezembraetzembretta.c: Access is restricted; consider a guided boat trip rather than disembarking independently.

archipeldelagalite.d: Volcanic archipelago off the northern coast of Tunisia, the country’s northernmost point. Protected area, former monk seal habitat.
archipeldelagalite.a: The volcanic archipelago off the northern coast of Tunisia, the country’s northernmost point, a former monk seal habitat, now a protected area.
archipeldelagalite.c: Access is by boat only and weather permitting: plan an organised excursion during the summer months from Bizerte or Tabarka.

ileskerkennah.d: A low-lying, sandy archipelago off the coast of Sfax, surrounded by shoals and wetlands. Traditional fishing using the ‘charfia’ method.
ileskerkennah.a: Traditional ‘charfia’ fishing; the ports of Sidi Youssef and Sidi Frej; the low-lying beaches and palm groves; the Bordj El Hassar.
ileskerkennah.c: A slow-paced, timeless atmosphere; hire a bike and sample the local grilled octopus.

ilededjerba.d: Tunisia’s largest island, in the Gulf of Gabès, connected to the mainland by an ancient causeway. A maritime oasis with lagoons.
ilededjerba.a: Tunisia’s largest island, a maritime oasis with lagoons, linked to the mainland by an ancient causeway.
ilededjerba.c: Hire a bike or a car to explore the island; the beaches and villages are well worth a visit.

ileskuriat.d: A small archipelago off the coast of Monastir, a nesting site for loggerhead sea turtles and a marine protected area.
ileskuriat.a: White sandy beaches and crystal-clear waters; the old lighthouse; the loggerhead turtle nesting site.
ileskuriat.c: A day trip from Monastir in season; take shade and water with you, as the island has no facilities.

ilotdechikly.d: A small islet in the middle of Lake Tunis, a nature reserve for birds and the site of a Hispano-Ottoman fort (Santiago).
ilotdechikly.a: The small bird sanctuary in the middle of the lake and the Hispano-Ottoman fort of Santiago which overlooks it.
ilotdechikly.c: Access is restricted and requires authorisation from the INP, with a boat crossing: this must be arranged in advance.

lacdetunis.d: A brackish lagoon between Tunis and the Gulf of Tunis, separated from the sea by a coastal sandbar. A wetland home to flamingos and waders.
lacdetunis.a: A lagoon on the outskirts of the capital: flamingos and waders around the islet of Chikly, which is home to the 16th-century Borj Chikly fort. The La Goulette road crosses the lake, offering views of Tunis; on the Lac 1 side, there is a landscaped promenade and waterside cafés.
lacdetunis.c: Birdwatching in winter; binoculars are useful; beautiful light in the morning from the shores. Borj Chikly (islet) can only be visited occasionally, by boat.

lacdebizerte.d: A coastal lagoon connected to the Mediterranean and Lake Ichkeul by channels. A sheltered body of water in the north of the country.
lacdebizerte.a: A vast coastal lagoon connected to the Mediterranean and Lake Ichkeul by channels. On its shores lie the old port of Bizerte, its kasbah and the canal – one of the most beautiful ports in the north.
lacdebizerte.c: Best explored by car or viewed from the shores; combine with the nearby Ichkeul Park and the old port of Bizerte.

oasisdetozeur.d: The Great Djerid Palm Grove on the shores of Chott el-Jerid, irrigated by a historic network of seguias. Coordinates centred on the town.
oasisdetozeur.a: The Great Djerid Palm Grove on the shores of Chott el-Jerid, irrigated by a historic network of seguias.
oasisdetozeur.c: A horse-drawn carriage ride or a walk through the palm grove, preferably in the morning.

oasisdenefta.d: The Djerid palm grove, renowned for the Corbeille de Nefta, the depression that is the source of the palm grove. Coordinates centred on the town.
oasisdenefta.a: The Djerid palm grove, famous for the Corbeille de Nefta, the depression that forms the source of the oasis.
oasisdenefta.c: The viewpoint overlooking the Corbeille offers the finest view; come at sunrise.

oasisdemontagnedechebika.d: A mountain oasis at the foot of Djebel el Negueb, fed by a spring and a waterfall. Coordinates centred on the village.
oasisdemontagnedechebika.a: A mountain oasis at the foot of Djebel el Negueb, fed by a spring and a waterfall.
oasisdemontagnedechebika.c: Path to the waterfall: wear sturdy footwear and visit in the morning before the heat sets in and the tourist groups arrive.

oasisdemontagnedetamerza.d: Tunisia’s largest mountain oasis, in the Djerid Mountains, with gorges and waterfalls. An old village abandoned after the floods of 1969.
oasisdemontagnedetamerza.a: Tunisia’s largest mountain oasis, with gorges, waterfalls and the old village abandoned after the floods of 1969.
oasisdemontagnedetamerza.c: Make sure you wear sturdy footwear for the gorges; the light and cooler temperatures are best in the morning.

oasisdemontagnedemides.d: A mountain oasis perched on the edge of spectacular canyons, near the Algerian border. Coordinates centred on the village.
oasisdemontagnedemides.a: An oasis perched on the edge of spectacular canyons, near the Algerian border.
oasisdemontagnedemides.c: Approach the canyon viewpoints with caution; the low-angle light enhances the landscape’s beauty.

oasisdeksarghilane.d: An isolated oasis on the edge of the Grand Erg Oriental, fed by a hot spring. Gateway to the Saharan desert.
oasisdeksarghilane.a: An isolated oasis on the edge of the Grand Erg Oriental, fed by a thermal spring, the gateway to the Sahara.
oasisdeksarghilane.c: Access via a track: 4x4 recommended; swimming possible at the spring, and sunsets over the dunes.

oasismaritimedegabes.d: A rare coastal oasis overlooking the sea directly, in the Gulf of Gabès. A terraced palm grove threatened by urbanisation and pollution. Coordinates centred on the town.
oasismaritimedegabes.a: A rare coastal oasis overlooking the sea directly; its terraced palm grove is now threatened by urbanisation and pollution.
oasismaritimedegabes.c: A stroll beneath the palm trees during the cooler hours; the condition of the oasis varies from one area to another.

chotteljerid.d: The largest salt lake in the Tunisian Sahara, dry for much of the year and covered in salt crusts. Mirages and colourful reflections.
chotteljerid.a: The largest salt lake in the Tunisian Sahara, dry for much of the year, covered in salt crusts and mirages.
chotteljerid.c: The road crosses the chott: stop at the designated viewing points at sunrise or sunset; the heat is stifling at midday.

chottelgharsa.d: A salt depression situated partly below sea level, north-west of Chott el-Jerid, near Tozeur.
chottelgharsa.a: A salt depression, partly below sea level, north-west of Chott el-Jerid near Tozeur.
chottelgharsa.c: The reflections and colours are at their most beautiful in low-angle light; stay on the trackable paths.

grandergoriental.d: A vast sea of Saharan dunes stretching across Algeria and south-western Tunisia (the Douz and Ksar Ghilane region). A spot located in Ksar Ghilane, the Tunisian gateway to the erg.
grandergoriental.a: A vast sea of Saharan dunes stretching as far as south-western Tunisia (Douz, Ksar Ghilane).
grandergoriental.c: A 4x4, guide and water are essential; the dunes are stunning at sunrise and sunset.

dunesdedouz.d: Nicknamed the ‘Gateway to the Sahara’, Douz provides access to the great dunes of the Grand Erg Oriental. Coordinates centred on the town.
dunesdedouz.a: The gateway to the Sahara: the vast dunes of the Grand Erg Oriental, accessible from Douz.
dunesdedouz.c: Camel treks or 4x4 trips at sunrise/sunset for the most beautiful light; extreme heat during the day.

capbon.d: A peninsula in north-eastern Tunisia with a rugged coastline between the Mediterranean Sea and the Gulf of Tunis. Coordinates at the northern tip of the cape.
capbon.a: A peninsula with a rugged coastline between the Mediterranean and the Gulf of Tunis, alternating between rocky headlands, beaches and villages; renowned as a migration corridor for birds of prey at its northern tip.
capbon.c: Ideal for a road trip (Korbous, El Haouaria, Kelibia); spring is the best time for observing migratory birds.

lagunedegharelmelh.d: A coastal lagoon and wetland at the foot of Djebel Nadhour, a Ramsar site renowned for its ramli gardens and birdlife. Coordinates centred on the village.
lagunedegharelmelh.a: The Ramsar lagoon and wetland at the foot of Djebel Nadhour, renowned for its traditional ramli gardens and birdlife.
lagunedegharelmelh.c: Beautiful light at the end of the day; bring binoculars for birdwatching and visit the town’s Ottoman forts whilst you’re there.

cotecoralliennedetabarka.d: The rocky coastline of Kroumirie, known for its ‘Aiguilles’ rock formations and coral reefs. Coordinates centred on the town.
cotecoralliennedetabarka.a: The ‘Aiguilles’ rocks; the Genoese fort; the coral reefs, popular with divers.
cotecoralliennedetabarka.c: A renowned diving spot; the jazz festival brings the town to life in summer.

capnegroparcnationaljebelchitanacapnegro.d: The Kroumirie Cape and Coastal National Park, combining coastal forest and sea cliffs in the north-west of the country.
capnegroparcnationaljebelchitanacapnegro.a: The cape and national park combine the Kroumirie coastal forest with sea cliffs in the north-west of the country.
capnegroparcnationaljebelchitanacapnegro.c: A wild and unspoilt site: make sure you have a suitable vehicle, plenty of water and are prepared for a walk to reach the viewpoints.

aindrahamkroumirie.d: A mountain resort in the heart of the Kroumirie cork oak forests, one of Tunisia’s rainiest regions. Coordinates centred on the town.
aindrahamkroumirie.a: The cork oak forests; houses with red-tiled roofs; footpaths and viewpoints overlooking the wooded mountains.
aindrahamkroumirie.c: The country’s rainiest region: lush and green in spring, sometimes snow-covered in winter – do bring a jacket.

montsdematmata.d: The Dahar range in southern Tunisia, known for its cave dwellings and arid landscapes. Coordinates centred on Matmata.
montsdematmata.a: The Dahar range, known for its cave dwellings and arid landscapes.
montsdematmata.c: Scenic but winding roads: drive carefully and carry water.

sourcesthermalesdekorbous.d: The Cap Bon spa resort, nestled in a coastal gorge, is fed by hot springs, including the Ain Atrous, which flows into the sea. Coordinates centred on the town.
sourcesthermalesdekorbous.a: The spa resort nestled in a coastal gorge; the Ain Atrous hot spring which flows into the sea.
sourcesthermalesdekorbous.c: Swimming is possible where the hot water meets the sea; a scenic road runs along the Cap Bon coastline.

hammambourguiba.d: A thermal spring in the Kroumirie forest area, near the Algerian border. Coordinates centred on the locality.
hammambourguiba.a: The thermal spring nestled in the Kroumirie forest, near the Algerian border.
hammambourguiba.c: A relaxing stop after forest walks; best combined with a visit to nearby Ain Draham.

djebelchambisommet.d: Tunisia’s highest peak (1,544 m), on the Tunisian mountain range near Kasserine. A forested massif of Aleppo pines, at the heart of a biosphere reserve.
djebelchambisommet.a: Tunisia’s highest peak (1,544 m) and its Aleppo pine forest, at the heart of a biosphere reserve.
djebelchambisommet.c: Climbing must be undertaken with a guide and a permit; check access conditions and set off early with plenty of water.

djebelghorra.d: Highest peak in the Kroumirie (1,250 m), on the Algerian-Tunisian border, the wettest area in Tunisia. Nature reserve established in 2010.
djebelghorra.a: The highest peak in the Kroumirie (1,250 m), the wettest area in Tunisia and a nature reserve, on the Algerian-Tunisian border.
djebelghorra.c: This hike is best undertaken in the warmer months; ensure you have suitable footwear, water and warm clothing, as the summit can be misty.

tabledejugurtha.d: Spectacular mesa (1,271 m) near Kalaat es Senam (Le Kef), a historic refuge attributed to Jugurtha. Granaries and cave dwellings; UNESCO tentative list.
tabledejugurtha.a: A spectacular mesa (1,271 m) accessible via a staircase carved into the rock, featuring granaries and cave dwellings, and offering sweeping panoramic views (UNESCO Tentative List).
tabledejugurtha.c: Set off in the morning on a clear day; allow 2 to 3 hours for the round trip from Kalaat es Senam, and take water and a hat with you.

djebelbireno.d: Tunisia’s second-highest peak (1,419 m), between Foussana and Thala (Kasserine). A forest of Aleppo pines from which zgougou is harvested.
djebelbireno.a: Tunisia’s second-highest peak (1,419 m) and its Aleppo pine forest, from which zgougou is harvested.
djebelbireno.c: Mountain hike between Foussana and Thala; allow a full day, and bring water and sturdy footwear.

djebelmghila.d: The Dorsale Mountain between Kasserine and Sidi Bouzid (1,370 m), at the heart of a national park established in 2010.
djebelmghila.a: The Dorsale Mountains (1,370 m) between Kasserine and Sidi Bouzid, at the heart of a national park established in 2010.
djebelmghila.c: Partly sensitive area: check access conditions before setting off on any hike.

djebelsemmama.d: A mountain in the Dorsale range in the governorate of Kasserine (1,314 m), aligned with Djebel Chambi.
djebelsemmama.a: A wooded mountain in the Dorsale range (1,314 m), aligned with Djebel Chambi.
djebelsemmama.c: Check access conditions before setting out on any hike in this area.

djebelserj.d: A limestone mountain, 1,357 m high, approximately 20 km south-east of Siliana. Ain Dhab Cave, forests of Aleppo pine and holm oak.
djebelserj.a: A limestone mountain (1,357 m) featuring the Ain Dhab Cave and forests of Aleppo pine and holm oak.
djebelserj.c: Approx. 20 km south-east of Siliana; a pleasant nature walk in spring – bring water and walking shoes.

djebelbargou.d: A mountain in the north-central region (1,266 m) south-east of Siliana, forming the western axis of the Dorsale range. Source of the Wadi Miliane.
djebelbargou.a: A mountain in the Dorsale range (1,266 m), source of the Miliane wadi, set in lush green surroundings.
djebelbargou.c: A lovely hiking area above Bargou; best visited in spring – do take water with you.

barragedesidisalem.d: Tunisia’s largest dam, completed in 1981 on the Medjerda near Testour (~555 million m³, reservoir area of 4,300 ha).
barragedesidisalem.a: The country’s largest dam on the Medjerda: a vast reservoir (~4,300 ha, ~555 million m³), offering sweeping views over the water and opportunities for freshwater fishing. Just a stone’s throw from Testour and its Andalusian medina.
barragedesidisalem.c: Beautiful panoramic views from the surrounding area; well worth combining with a visit to Testour (mosque with an Andalusian minaret). An easy day trip from Béja or Medjez el-Bab.

barragedebenimtir.d: Dam built between 1946 and 1953 on the Oued El Lil to the south-west of Ain Draham, in the wooded Kroumirie region. Irrigation, drinking water, hydroelectricity.
barragedebenimtir.a: A 1950s dam on the El Lil wadi, nestled in the cork oak forest of Kroumirie, south-west of Aïn Draham — one of Tunisia’s greenest landscapes.
barragedebenimtir.c: A lovely spot for a panoramic stop on the road to Ain Draham; a lush setting in spring, sometimes misty and cool in winter.

barragedebouheurtma.d: North-western dam (Jendouba), with the raising of the dam completed in 2024, bringing the capacity to ~145 million m³.
barragedebouheurtma.a: The North-West Dam and its reservoir, in the Jendouba region.
barragedebouheurtma.c: A nature stop on the region’s roads; best combined with visits to nearby ancient sites.

barragemellegue.d: A 65-metre multi-arch dam on the Mellegue wadi, built between 1949 and 1956 (Le Kef). Irrigation, flood control, hydroelectricity.
barragemellegue.a: A large 65-metre multi-arch dam (1949–1956) on the Mellegue wadi, set in a steep-sided wadi landscape.
barragemellegue.c: Best visited in conjunction with the nearby village of Nebeur; pleasant views, no tourist facilities.

barragedesidielbarrak.d: Earth-fill dam (~265 million m³) completed around 2000 (Beja), near Tabarka. Ramsar wetland.
barragedesidielbarrak.a: Large earth-fill dam near Tabarka, alongside a Ramsar-designated wetland: a reservoir ideal for observing waterbirds, in the wooded hinterland of Nefza.
barragedesidielbarrak.c: Observe the birdlife around the reservoir; a nature stop-off on the road between Nefza and Tabarka. Check with local authorities before venturing off the tracks.

barragelakhmess.d: A 32-metre gravity dam, inaugurated in 1966 on the Lakhmess wadi, approximately 15 km south-east of Siliana, at the foot of Djebel Serj.
barragelakhmess.a: A 32-metre gravity dam (1966) on the Lakhmess wadi, at the foot of Djebel Serj.
barragelakhmess.c: Scenic stop-off point ~15 km south-east of Siliana, to be combined with a visit to Djebel Serj.

djebelressas.d: An isolated limestone massif (~795 m) south-east of Tunis, a landmark of Greater Tunis. Former lead mines (the name means ‘lead mountain’). Approximate coordinates.
djebelressas.a: The iconic limestone silhouette to the south-east of Tunis, with its cliffs, old lead mine tunnels and panoramic views from the heights.
djebelressas.c: A hike for experienced walkers; set off early, take water and wear sturdy footwear; views over Greater Tunis from the summit.

sebkhetariana.d: A brackish lagoon north of Tunis, separated from the sea by a sand dune ridge. A wetland home to flamingos and waterbirds.
sebkhetariana.a: The brackish lagoon north of Tunis and its birdlife, notably flamingos and waterbirds.
sebkhetariana.c: Birdwatching from the surrounding area; good light at dawn, binoculars recommended.

sebkhetsejoumi.d: A vast salt pan to the south-west of Tunis, filled with water in winter. An important wetland for birdlife, threatened by urbanisation.
sebkhetsejoumi.a: The vast salt depression south-west of Tunis, flooded in winter, frequented by numerous waterbirds.
sebkhetsejoumi.c: Best visited in winter when it is flooded; birdwatching from the surrounding area, avoiding degraded urbanised zones.

capangelarasbensakka.d: A headland on the northern coast of Bizerte, considered the northernmost point of the African continent. Cliffs and wild coastline.
capangelarasbensakka.a: The headland is regarded as the northernmost point of the African continent, with its cliffs and wild coastline.
capangelarasbensakka.c: Visit for the symbolic significance of Africa’s northernmost point and the panoramic views; the final stretch of track is rough, so ensure you have a suitable vehicle.

capblancrasalabiad.d: A promontory of white limestone on the coast of Bizerte, long presented as the northernmost point of Africa, near Cape Angela.
capblancrasalabiad.a: The white limestone promontory overlooking the sea, near Cape Angela, long presented as the northernmost point of Africa.
capblancrasalabiad.c: Combine with nearby Cape Angela; beautiful light and views of the coast at the end of the day.

capzebib.d: A rocky headland on the north-eastern coast of Bizerte, extending into a series of small islets. An area of cliffs and fishing.
capzebib.a: The rocky headland on the north-eastern coast of Bizerte, extending into a series of small islets, in an area of cliffs and fishing grounds.
capzebib.c: A peaceful coastal stop; best combined with the other headlands in the north of Bizerte.

capserrat.d: A headland and sandy cove on the Kroumirie coast (Bizerte), nestled between woodland and a lagoon, dominated by a lighthouse. A preserved stretch of coastline.
capserrat.a: The headland and its sandy cove, situated between the forest and the lagoon and overlooked by a lighthouse, on the unspoilt Kroumirie coastline.
capserrat.c: An ideal wild beach in summer; the access road is long, so bring provisions and water as there are few facilities.

ilescani.d: A small rocky archipelago off the northern coast of Bizerte, topped by a lighthouse. A nesting site for seabirds.
ilescani.a: The small rocky archipelago topped by a lighthouse, off the north coast of Bizerte, a nesting site for seabirds.
ilescani.c: Accessible only by boat and weather permitting; best visited as part of an organised boat trip.

djebelichkeul.d: An isolated limestone mountain overlooking Lake Ichkeul, within the national park. Mediterranean flora and fauna, with thermal springs at its foot.
djebelichkeul.a: The isolated limestone mountain overlooking the lake, with its Mediterranean flora and fauna and the hot springs at its foot.
djebelichkeul.c: Hike up the park’s trails for views of the lake; binoculars are useful, and the best time to visit is from autumn to spring.

embouchuredelamedjerda.d: The delta and mouth of the Medjerda, Tunisia’s main river, on the north coast near Kalaat el-Andalous. Alluvial plain and coastal wetland.
embouchuredelamedjerda.a: The delta of Tunisia’s main river, its alluvial plain and the coastal wetland rich in birdlife, near Kalaat el-Andalous.
embouchuredelamedjerda.c: Combine this with a visit to the hilltop village of Kalaat el-Andalous; an excellent spot for birdwatching.

sebkhadekelbia.d: An intermittent salt lake (~8,000 ha) in the Kairouan plain, north of the city. The second-largest wetland after Ichkeul, a nature reserve since 1993. Approximate coordinates.
sebkhadekelbia.a: An intermittent salt lake (~8,000 ha) north of Kairouan, a nature reserve and a major wetland for waterbirds after Ichkeul.
sebkhadekelbia.c: Of particular interest to birdwatchers after the rains, when the lake is full; binoculars recommended.

sebkhethalkelmenzel.d: Coastal salt lagoon in the governorate of Sousse, near Sidi Khelifa. Ramsar wetland (~1,450 ha), important for birdlife. Approximate coordinates.
sebkhethalkelmenzel.a: Coastal salt lagoon (~1,450 ha) near Sidi Khelifa, a Ramsar wetland of international importance for birdlife.
sebkhethalkelmenzel.c: Undeveloped natural site; approach with discretion whilst observing birds.

ilezembretta.d: Small islet in the Gulf of Tunis, ~8 km east of Zembra (~2 ha). Together with Zembra, it forms an important area for the conservation of seabirds.
ilezembretta.a: Small islet (~2 ha) to the east of Zembra, forming, together with it, a key area for the conservation of seabirds.
ilezembretta.c: Protected islet with restricted access; observation from the sea only.

foretdedarchichou.d: Cap Bon State Forest (>6,000 ha) north of El Haouaria (Nabeul). A Mediterranean dune forest resulting from dune stabilisation work begun around 1930.
foretdedarchichou.a: A state-owned dune forest covering more than 6,000 ha north of El Haouaria, resulting from the stabilisation of the Cap Bon dunes which began around 1930.
foretdedarchichou.c: A pleasant setting for a nature break between the capes; please stay on the tracks.

djebelorbatasommet.d: A limestone mountain (1,165 m) east of Gafsa, stretching some 60 km to the north-east. The landscape is protected by the national park. Approximate coordinates.
djebelorbatasommet.a: A limestone mountain rising to 1,165 m east of Gafsa, protected by the national park.
djebelorbatasommet.c: Climb reserved for walkers: set off early in the morning, take water and wear sturdy footwear.

gorgesdeselja.d: A steep-sided valley several km long through which the Selja wadi flows, between Metlaoui and Redeyef (Gafsa). A nature reserve (675 ha) since 2009, crossed by the Red Lizard.
gorgesdeselja.a: The steep-sided valley of the Selja wadi between Metlaoui and Redeyef, a nature reserve through which the Lezard Rouge railway runs.
gorgesdeselja.c: The train is the best way to explore the gorges; book in advance during peak season.

oasisdegafsa.d: Historic oasis system (~700 ha) on the northern edge of the Sahara (Sakdoud, Ksar, Lela, Gafsa, El Guettar), featuring three-tiered terraced farming. Recognised as a GIAHS in 2011.
oasisdegafsa.a: Historic oasis system with three-tiered terraced farming, recognised as a Global Important Agricultural Heritage System (GIAHS, 2011).
oasisdegafsa.c: A stroll through the palm grove during the cooler hours of the day; a guide explains the irrigation system.

sebkhetennoual.d: Vast salt depression in the central steppe (~17,000 ha), on the border between Sidi Bouzid and Sfax. A Ramsar wetland since 2007.
sebkhetennoual.a: A vast salt depression in the central steppe (~17,000 ha), a Ramsar wetland on the border between Sidi Bouzid and Sfax, frequented by waterbirds.
sebkhetennoual.c: Ornithological interest: binoculars are useful, and avoid walking on the salt crusts.

maraissalantsdethynasfax.d: Salt pans and coastal wetland south of Sfax, along the Gulf of Gabès near Thyna. Large protected wetland, designated a Ramsar site in 2007, important for waterbirds. Approximate coordinates.
maraissalantsdethynasfax.a: Salt pans and coastal wetland south of Sfax (Ramsar), important for flamingos and waterbirds.
maraissalantsdethynasfax.c: Bring binoculars; observe from the dykes without disturbing the birds.

corbeilledenefta.d: A natural basket-shaped depression beneath the Nefta hills, fed by springs that irrigate the original oasis. An iconic site in the Djerid.
corbeilledenefta.a: A natural basket-shaped depression beneath the Nefta hills, fed by springs that irrigate the original oasis.
corbeilledenefta.c: The viewpoint offers the finest view; come at sunrise to catch the light.

palmeraiededouz.d: A vast palm grove (>500,000 palm trees) encircling Douz, the gateway to the Sahara (Kebili). Coordinates centred on the town.
palmeraiededouz.a: A vast palm grove of over 500,000 palm trees encircling Douz, the gateway to the Sahara.
palmeraiededouz.c: A shaded stroll through the palm grove; combine it with an excursion to the nearby dunes.

chottelfejaj.d: A long, muddy, endorheic lake arm extending eastwards from Chott el-Jerid, north of Nefzaoua. It dries up for much of the year.
chottelfejaj.a: A long, salt-encrusted endorheic lake extending eastwards from Chott el-Jerid; it dries up for much of the year.
chottelfejaj.c: Unmanaged salt flat: stay on the safe tracks and avoid the crust after rainfall.

djebeldahar.d: Southeast mountain range (~713 m, ~6,500 km²), Tataouine and Medenine regions. An arid plateau dotted with hilltop Berber villages and ksour.
djebeldahar.a: Arid plateau in the south-east, dotted with hilltop Berber villages and ksour, in the regions of Tataouine and Medenine.
djebeldahar.c: An ideal region for a tour of the ksour; a 4x4 or guide is useful for the tracks.

djebeltebaga.d: Mountain range north of Chott el-Jerid near Kebili, featuring fossilised reefs from the Permian marine period. Site of the Tebaga breakthrough (Battle of the Mareth Line, 1943).
djebeltebaga.a: Mountain range north of Chott el-Jerid with Permian fossil reefs; site of the Tebaga breakthrough (1943).
djebeltebaga.c: Of geological and historical interest; arid terrain – bring water and a hat.

elhammadujerid.d: Oasis town in the governorate of Tozeur, on the northern edge of the Djerid, with hot springs. Palm grove irrigated by thermal springs.
elhammadujerid.a: Oasis town on the northern edge of the Djerid, irrigated by hot springs.
elhammadujerid.c: Very hot springs: enquire about the pools accessible to visitors.

lagunedekorbasebkhakorba.d: Coastal lagoon north of Korba, an important wetland for migratory birds of Cap Bon.
lagunedekorbasebkhakorba.a: Coastal lagoon north of Korba, an important wetland for migratory birds of Cap Bon.
lagunedekorbasebkhakorba.c: Birdwatching site; the migration periods are the best times to visit; binoculars are useful.

sebkhetsoliman.d: Soliman Sebkha, a wetland in Cap Bon and a Ramsar site of importance for waterbirds.
sebkhetsoliman.a: Cap Bon wetland designated as a Ramsar site, important for waterbirds.
sebkhetsoliman.c: Of primarily ornithological interest; observe from a distance so as not to disturb the birds.

sebkhaelmaamourah.d: Sebkha El Maâmourah, a coastal wetland to the south-east of Cap Bon.
sebkhaelmaamourah.a: Coastal wetland to the south-east of Cap Bon.
sebkhaelmaamourah.c: A modest natural site, mainly for observing waterbirds.

sebkhatazerka.d: Sebkha Tazerka, a wetland on the east coast of Cap Bon.
sebkhatazerka.a: Wetland on the east coast of Cap Bon.
sebkhatazerka.c: An unassuming birding spot; few facilities on site.

grottedeschauvessouriselhaouaria.d: Bat cave near El Haouaria, at the tip of Cap Bon.
grottedeschauvessouriselhaouaria.a: A cave harbouring bats, near El Haouaria at the tip of Cap Bon.
grottedeschauvessouriselhaouaria.c: Best visited in combination with the nearby Roman quarries; a torch and suitable footwear are recommended.

djebelhammamet.d: Coastal range to the south-west of Hammamet.
djebelhammamet.a: Coastal mountain range to the south-west of Hammamet overlooking the bay.
djebelhammamet.c: A short hike offering scenic views; set off early to avoid the heat.

djebelelhaouaria.d: Terrain at the northern tip of Cap Bon, an important migration corridor for birds of prey. Approximate coordinates.
djebelelhaouaria.a: Terrain at the northern tip of Cap Bon, an important migration corridor for birds of prey.
djebelelhaouaria.c: Spring is the best time of year to observe the passage of birds of prey; binoculars are essential.

sebkhadesidielhanisousse.d: Large salt lake (~36,000 ha) south-west of Sousse. A salt flat subject to periodic flooding.
sebkhadesidielhanisousse.a: Large salt lake (~36,000 ha) south-west of Sousse, a salt flat subject to periodic flooding.
sebkhadesidielhanisousse.c: A salt landscape that changes with the seasons; an undeveloped natural site.

sebkhademoknine.d: A salt depression south-east of Moknine, a wetland of interest for birdlife.
sebkhademoknine.a: A salt depression south-east of Moknine, a wetland of interest for birdlife.
sebkhademoknine.c: Of ornithological interest; worth combining with a visit to Moknine.

maraissalantsdemonastir.d: Wetland (~1,000 ha) designated a Ramsar site in 2012, important for pink flamingos.
maraissalantsdemonastir.a: A wetland of around 1,000 ha designated a Ramsar site in 2012, important for pink flamingos.
maraissalantsdemonastir.c: A good spot for observing flamingos; come early in the morning with binoculars.

ileconigliera.d: A small island off the coast of the Gulf of Monastir, part of the Kuriat archipelago.
ileconigliera.a: A small island off the Gulf of Monastir, part of the Kuriat archipelago.
ileconigliera.c: It can only be reached by sea, as part of an excursion to the Kuriat Islands.

chottouladamar.d: A salt flat (chott) in the Bekalta region, near Ras Dimass.
chottouladamar.a: A salt flat (chott) in the Bekalta region, near Ras Dimass.
chottouladamar.c: An undeveloped natural site; worth visiting, perhaps in conjunction with the nearby ruins of Thapsus.

bahiretelbibane.d: Large south-eastern coastal lagoon (Medenine), a Ramsar site since 2007, important for fishing and birdlife.
bahiretelbibane.a: Large south-eastern coastal lagoon, a Ramsar site important for fishing and birdlife.
bahiretelbibane.c: Binoculars are useful for birdwatching; light is best early in the morning.

sebkhetelmelahdezarzis.d: Vast salt sebkha near Zarzis (~150 km²), separated from the sea by a dune ridge, exploited for salt.
sebkhetelmelahdezarzis.a: Vast salt sebkha (~150 km²) near Zarzis, separated from the sea by a dune ridge and used for salt production.
sebkhetelmelahdezarzis.c: Photogenic reflections in low-angle light; stay on the accessible paths.

golfedegabespetitesyrte.d: A large gulf on the south-east coast opening onto the Mediterranean, formerly known as Petite Syrte, with a significant tidal range.
golfedegabespetitesyrte.a: A large gulf on the south-east coast, the ancient Petite Syrte, notable for its significant tidal range.
golfedegabespetitesyrte.c: The tidal range exposes much of the foreshore: check the tide times for the seaside.

ouedakarit.d: A coastal watercourse north of Gabès flowing into the gulf, a site of prehistoric significance.
ouedakarit.a: A coastal watercourse north of Gabès, notable for its prehistory and the site of a battle in 1943.
ouedakarit.c: Site with no tourist facilities: of mainly historical and natural interest.

djebelbouramli.d: A mountain in the south-west (Gafsa), extending from Djebel Orbata and bordering the Gafsa plain.
djebelbouramli.a: A mountain in the south-west extending from Djebel Orbata and bordering the Gafsa plain.
djebelbouramli.c: Arid terrain: suitable only for well-equipped walkers, with water supplies and an early start.

ainkriz.d: Natural spring north of Tozeur, in the El Oudiane oasis group (Jerid).
ainkriz.a: Natural spring north of Tozeur, in the El Oudiane oasis group (Jerid).
ainkriz.c: A refreshing stop in the palm grove; please respect the spring’s facilities.

phareducapangela.d: Lighthouse marking Cape Angela (Ras ben Sakka), the northernmost point of mainland Africa.
phareducapangela.a: The lighthouse marking Cape Angela (Ras ben Sakka), the northernmost point of mainland Africa.
phareducapangela.c: A landmark marking the tip of the continent; combine your visit with Cape Angela and Cape Blanc.

capsidialielmekki.d: A rocky headland (formerly Cape Farina) enclosing Ghar el Melh Bay, a popular beach and an Ottoman fort.
capsidialielmekki.a: The rocky headland enclosing Ghar el Melh Bay, with its popular beach and Ottoman fort, formerly known as Cape Farina.
capsidialielmekki.c: A beautiful beach that gets very busy in summer: arrive early, and combine your visit with Raf Raf and the Ghar el Melh lagoon.

iledelagaliteileprincipale.d: The largest island in the volcanic La Galite archipelago, a nature reserve rich in birdlife and flora.
iledelagaliteileprincipale.a: The largest island in the volcanic La Galite archipelago, a nature reserve rich in birdlife and flora.
iledelagaliteileprincipale.c: Access by boat during the summer months only; book an organised excursion and check the weather forecast.

legaliton.d: A rocky islet in the La Galite archipelago featuring a lighthouse, the westernmost point of Tunisia.
legaliton.a: The rocky islet with a lighthouse, Tunisia’s westernmost point, in the La Galite archipelago.
legaliton.c: A remote site out at sea: best viewed during a boat trip around La Galite.

ilepilau.d: A small island off the coast of Raf Raf and Cape Sidi Ali el-Mekki.
ilepilau.a: The small island off the coast of Raf Raf and Cape Sidi Ali el-Mekki, with a distinctive silhouette facing the beach.
ilepilau.c: Best viewed from Raf Raf beach; there are no visitor facilities on the island.

ileplane.d: A low-lying island off Cape Sidi Ali el-Mekki, topped by a lighthouse.
ileplane.a: The low-lying island topped by a lighthouse, off Cape Sidi Ali el-Mekki.
ileplane.c: Visible from the coast; well worth including in a tour of Ghar el Melh Bay.

ilesfratelli.d: A small rocky archipelago off the north-west coast, between Cape Serrat and Cape Negro.
ilesfratelli.a: The small rocky archipelago off the north-west coast, between Cape Serrat and Cape Negro.
ilesfratelli.c: A navigational mark visible from the Kroumirie coastline; no landing permitted.

garaasejnane.d: North-western wetland (marsh) near Sejnane, important for migratory birdlife.
garaasejnane.a: The wetland and marsh near Sejnane, important for migratory birds.
garaasejnane.c: Visit during the wet season for waterbirds; binoculars recommended, to be combined with a visit to the town of Sejnane.

barragedejoumine.d: Reservoir feeding Lake Ichkeul, in the south-west of the governorate.
barragedejoumine.a: The reservoir feeding Lake Ichkeul, in the south-west of the governorate of Bizerte.
barragedejoumine.c: A nature stop linked to the Ichkeul water system; worth seeing on the way to the park.

barragedesejnane.d: Dam and reservoir on the Sejnane wadi, in the north-west of the governorate.
barragedesejnane.a: The dam and its reservoir on the Sejnane wadi, in the north-west of the governorate.
barragedesejnane.c: Panoramic viewpoint on the road to Sejnane; worth combining with a visit to the neighbouring wetlands.

barragedekasseb.d: Dam to the west of Beja, supplying drinking water to Greater Tunis, at the foot of the Kroumirie.
barragedekasseb.a: The dam west of Béja, which supplies Greater Tunis with drinking water, at the foot of the Kroumirie.
barragedekasseb.c: A leafy stop in spring; a stop-off on the forest roads of the Béja region.

djebelkhroufa.d: Mountain and nature reserve in the Nefza region, a forested massif in the north-west.
djebelkhroufa.a: The mountain and nature reserve in the Nefza region, a forested massif in the north-west.
djebelkhroufa.c: A pleasant forest walk in spring and autumn; bring water and sturdy footwear.

aiguillesdetabarka.d: Remarkable rock formation on the Tabarka coast: sandstone spires rising from the seashore.
aiguillesdetabarka.a: The sandstone spires rising from the seashore, an iconic rock formation on the Tabarka coast.
aiguillesdetabarka.c: A great spot for photos at sunset; well worth combining with a visit to the Genoese fort and the coral coast.

parcnationaldeouedzen.d: Kroumirie National Park, protecting the Zen oak forest and the Barbary deer, south of Tabarka.
parcnationaldeouedzen.a: The Kroumirie oak forest and the Barbary deer it protects, south of Tabarka.
parcnationaldeouedzen.c: Best visited in spring or autumn; you’ll need a vehicle and to walk to reach the forest.

tourbieresdedarfatma.d: Kroumirie High-Altitude Peat Bogs Nature Reserve, a rare wetland in Tunisia. Approximate coordinates.
tourbieresdedarfatma.a: The high-altitude peat bogs of Kroumirie, a rare wetland in Tunisia, within a nature reserve.
tourbieresdedarfatma.c: A sensitive natural site with few facilities: walk with care, ideally with a guide, in spring.

reservenaturelledainzana.d: Kroumirie Nature Reserve near Ghardimaou, with its oak stands and forest biodiversity.
reservenaturelledainzana.a: The oak woodland and forest biodiversity of Kroumirie, near Ghardimaou.
reservenaturelledainzana.c: A nature stop to combine with Ghardimaou and El Feija Park; best visited in spring.

barragebarbara.d: Dam and reservoir in Kroumirie, on the Oued el Kebir.
barragebarbara.a: The dam and its reservoir in Kroumirie, on the Oued el Kebir, set in wooded surroundings.
barragebarbara.c: Panoramic viewpoint along the forest roads of the north-west; lush green surroundings during the wet season.

djebelousselat.d: Limestone mountain in the Tunisian mountain range, the highest point in the governorate of Kairouan (Oueslatia).
djebelousselat.a: Limestone mountain in the Tunisian mountain range, the highest point in the Kairouan governorate, in the Oueslatia region.
djebelousselat.c: Mid-mountain hike: make sure you wear suitable footwear and take plenty of water.

djebeltrozza.d: Mountain range in the Kairouan governorate, near Haffouz.
djebeltrozza.a: Mountain range in the Kairouan governorate, near Haffouz.
djebeltrozza.c: Rural, largely undeveloped landscape: make sure you bring water and wear suitable footwear.

sebkhatsaacha.d: Sebkha (salt flat) in the south of the Kairouan governorate.
sebkhatsaacha.a: Salt flat (sebkha) in the south of the Kairouan governorate.
sebkhatsaacha.c: A wetland best viewed from a distance; avoid venturing onto the salt crust.

rasdjezirachebba.d: Coastal headland in the south of the governorate, near Chebba.
rasdjezirachebba.a: Coastal headland in the south of the Mahdia governorate, near Chebba.
rasdjezirachebba.c: A pleasant seaside viewpoint; wear sturdy footwear on the rocks.

rassalakta.a: Salakta headland, near the ancient site of the same name.
rassalakta.c: Best combined with a visit to the Salakta site and museum.

sebkhaelghorra.d: Sebkha (temporary salt lake) to the west of the Mahdia governorate.
sebkhaelghorra.a: Temporary salt lake (sebkha) in the west of the Mahdia governorate.
sebkhaelghorra.c: A wetland best viewed from a distance, particularly during the wet season.

sebkhacherita.d: Sebkha in the west of the Mahdia governorate.
sebkhacherita.a: Sebkha in the west of the Mahdia governorate.
sebkhacherita.c: Naturalist’s interest: observe waterbirds without venturing onto the salt flats.

sebkhabenghiadha.c: Wetland best viewed from the surrounding area; binoculars recommended.

reservenaturelledjebelrihanadjebelgouleb.d: Nature reserve (~2,000 ha) covering the Djebels Rihana and Goulebe, Souk Jedid district.
reservenaturelledjebelrihanadjebelgouleb.a: Nature reserve of approximately 2,000 ha covering the Rihana and Goulebe djebels, in the Souk Jedid district.
reservenaturelledjebelrihanadjebelgouleb.c: Access to the reserve: check the conditions before visiting.

plainedegammouda.d: The Gammouda agricultural plain, in the central part of the governorate of Sidi Bouzid.
plainedegammouda.a: Agricultural plain in the central part of the governorate of Sidi Bouzid.
plainedegammouda.c: Rural landscape rather than a tourist site: to be passed through along the road.

djebelchlel.d: Mountains in the east of the Sidi Bouzid governorate, near Ouled Haffouz.
djebelchlel.a: Mountains in the east of the Sidi Bouzid governorate, near Ouled Haffouz.
djebelchlel.c: A largely unspoilt natural setting: make sure you bring water and sturdy footwear.

ileskneiss.d: Archipelago and nature reserve (Ramsar) in the Gulf of Gabès, important for migratory birds.
ileskneiss.a: Archipelago and Ramsar nature reserve in the Gulf of Gabès, important for migratory birds.
ileskneiss.c: Protected area: access by sea; arrangements to be made locally whilst respecting the birdlife.

reservenaturelledelgonna.d: Nature reserve and protected area in the governorate of Sfax.
reservenaturelledelgonna.a: Nature reserve and protected area in the governorate of Sfax.
reservenaturelledelgonna.c: Access to the reserve: check the conditions before visiting.

plagedechaffar.d: Beach on the coast of the Gulf of Gabès, south of Sfax.
plagedechaffar.a: Beach on the Gulf of Gabès, south of Sfax.
plagedechaffar.c: A place for swimming and relaxation; check conditions on site.

sebkhaeljem.d: Salt flat (sebkha) in the north of the Sfax Governorate, near El Jem.
sebkhaeljem.a: Salt flat (sebkha) in the north of the Sfax governorate, near El Jem.
sebkhaeljem.c: A wetland best observed from a distance, particularly during the wet season.

zoneshumidesdelaskhira.d: Wetland complex in the south of the Sfax governorate (Chott el Guetayate, Akarit/Rekhama/Meleh wadis), important for birdlife.
zoneshumidesdelaskhira.a: Wetland complex in the south of the Sfax governorate (Chott el Guetayate, the Akarit, Rekhama and Meleh wadis), important for birdlife.
zoneshumidesdelaskhira.c: Ornithological interest: binoculars recommended; birdwatching from a distance.

djebeldyrdyrelkef.d: A table mountain in the Tunisian Atlas (approx. 1,074 m) overlooking the town of Le Kef, built on its cliff face.
djebeldyrdyrelkef.a: A table mountain (approx. 1,074 m) overlooking the town of Le Kef, built on its cliff face, offering sweeping panoramic views.
djebeldyrdyrelkef.c: Climb up to the viewpoint overlooking El Kef and the plain, preferably in the late afternoon.

barragedesiliana.d: A dam on the Siliana wadi, used for irrigation and water supply.
barragedesiliana.a: A dam on the Siliana wadi, set against a backdrop of plains and hills.
barragedesiliana.c: A simple scenic stop near Siliana.

parcnationaldechambi.d: A national park established in 1980 around Djebel Chambi, a UNESCO biosphere reserve.
parcnationaldechambi.a: The national park, established in 1980 around Djebel Chambi, a UNESCO biosphere reserve and the country’s highest peak.
parcnationaldechambi.c: Restricted access: check permits and safety arrangements before your visit, and allow a full day.

parcdubelvedere.d: Tunis’s largest and oldest urban park (1892), situated on a wooded hill overlooking the city and the lake.
parcdubelvedere.a: The largest park in Tunis on its wooded hill; the Ottoman koubba; the panoramic view of the city and the lake.
parcdubelvedere.c: A pleasant morning stroll in the shade of olive and pine trees, in the heart of Tunis.

capcarthage.d: A rocky headland on the northern coast of Tunis, north of Sidi Bou Said and La Marsa.
capcarthage.a: The rocky headland on the coast north of Sidi Bou Said and La Marsa, with its views of the sea and the coastline.
capcarthage.c: Beautiful light at sunset; best combined with a stroll in Sidi Bou Said or La Marsa.

capgammarth.d: A headland on the coast north of La Marsa, with the cliffs and beaches of Gammarth.
capgammarth.a: The cliffs and beaches of Gammarth north of La Marsa, and panoramic coastal views of the gulf.
capgammarth.c: A lovely spot for a seaside stroll; picturesque sunsets over the coast.

parcennahli.d: A vast urban park and reforested area on the hills north of Tunis (Ariana), with a viewpoint overlooking the city.
parcennahli.a: The extensive reforested area on the hills north of Tunis and its panoramic viewpoint over the city and the lake.
parcennahli.c: A popular spot for Sunday walks and picnics; unobstructed views on clear days.

djebelboukornine.d: A mountain with twin peaks (‘the two horns’) overlooking Hammam Lif and the Gulf of Tunis.
djebelboukornine.a: The distinctive twin peaks (‘the two horns’) overlooking Hammam Lif, its wooded paths and the view of the Gulf of Tunis.
djebelboukornine.c: Hike through the heart of the national park; set off from Hammam Lif – bring water and sturdy walking shoes.

djebelmarchana.d: The southern Ben Arous hills form a nature reserve, home to Mediterranean flora and fauna.
djebelmarchana.a: The wooded hills of southern Ben Arous, designated as a nature reserve, with its Mediterranean flora and fauna.
djebelmarchana.c: A nature site with few facilities for walkers; check access details and bring water.

sebkhaderades.d: A salt marsh on the southern edge of Lake Tunis, near Rades, a peri-urban wetland.
sebkhaderades.a: The peri-urban salt marsh on the southern edge of Lake Tunis, frequented by waterbirds.
sebkhaderades.c: Wetland in an urbanised area: observation from the surrounding area; of particular ornithological interest in winter.

sebkhakourzia.d: Large sebkha in the west of the Zaghouan governorate (El Fahs region), a seasonal wetland.
sebkhakourzia.a: The large seasonal sebkha in western Zaghouan (El Fahs region) with its salt flats and marshes, depending on the season.
sebkhakourzia.c: Best viewed after rainfall when it is flooded; birdwatching from the surrounding area.
